articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Preorders Are Live
articles.summary: Everything you need to know to preorder Grand Theft Auto 6 for PS5 or Xbox Series X|S.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 , the most anticipated game of the year and possibly of all time, is now officially up for preorder on PS5 and Xbox , priced at $79.99 digitally or via an online retailer, alongside the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition, priced at $99.99.

We've gathered all the information you might need in order to make an informed purchase, along with links to where you can preorder the game today.

Grand Theft Auto 6 - PS5 Physical (Code in Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Xbox Physical (Code in Box)

Update: Amazon has reopened preorders for the standard edition of Grand Theft Auto 6 after briefly selling out. The Ultimate Edition is available only through PlayStation Store and Xbox Store digital preorders.

Priced from $79.99 , preorders for "physical" copies of Grand Theft Auto 6 are available now — though you'll only get a box containing a digital download code .

Physical copies will actually be available from November 12, a full week ahead of the game's full launch on November 19. That's also when GTA 6 pre-loading will become available , allowing anyone with a physical copy or digital pre-order to get the game downloading.

Note that some retailers like Amazon won't charge you for your purchase until it eventually ships, so if you're looking to save up over the second half of the year, picking up a physical copy is likely your best bet.

GTA 6 Preorder Bonus - The Vintage Vice City Pack

The Vintage Vice City Pack is included with all digital purchases of GTA 6 made prior to November 20, 2026, and with preorders of the physical version of GTA 6 while supplies last.

GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Screenshots

’55 Vapid Stanier and Shore Court Garage: Cruise Shore Drive in the legendary ’55 Vapid Stanier, a Vice City classic meant to be admired, and store it in a new personal garage just a stone’s throw from the glistening sands of Ocean Beach. Like all personal garages in Leonida, you’ll have a weapon locker to customize your loadout for any occasion plus a secure place to deposit stolen goods for the local Fence, who will accept most stolen goods at a reasonably discounted rate.

Outfits and Hairstyles: Dress for excess with two Vice City luxury looks for both Jason and Lucia:

Jason: An effortlessly chic linen suit in vintage pastel, complemented by the cut and coif of the decade of decadence.

Lucia: The world is yours in a red sequin mini dress and curls.

Exclusive Weapon Pattern: Channel the original Vice City kingpin, Tommy Vercetti, and his iconic palm tree button-up with a tropical pattern available to adorn most guns.

Preorder Grand Theft Auto 6 - Ultimate Edition

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Ultimate Edition (Digital)

Grand Theft Auto 6's Ultimate Edition adds exclusive vehicles, weapon variants, customization options, side activities, and a large collection of cosmetic content for both protagonists. It costs $100 and is available as a digital or physical purchase.

Vapid Dominator Buggy with access to the Paradise Garage, including a weapon locker and stash box.

'95 Grotti Cheetah sports car with a retro-inspired design.

Dinka Enduro motorcycle, Crest Kayak, and exclusive Vapid Ganado pickup truck upgrades at Jason's Safehouse.

Shitzu Squalo speedboat equipped with a weapons crate.

Access to two exclusive vehicle customization shops: Rideout Customs (Vice City) One-Eyed Willie's (Lake Leonida)

Classic Car Collection side activity featuring restoration projects, including four Ultimate Edition-exclusive vehicles.

Hawk & Little Morgan Revolver with unique Vice City-themed designs for Jason and Lucia.

Personalized versions of Jason's Girardi ES9 pistol and Lucia's Klose K17 pistol.

PTT Youngin$ Compound content, including a special robbery opportunity and exclusive contraband rewards.

Exclusive outfits, tattoos, and accessories for Jason and Lucia.

Access to Stock 305, an exclusive streetwear store.

Exclusive hairstyles, makeup, nails, and facial hair options from Sara's Unisex Salon.

Over 50 exclusive tattoos from Electric Fang Tattoo.

Free $50 Best Buy Gift Card When Buying GTA 6 + Eligible Console

Free $50 Best Buy Gift Card with GTA 6 + Console Purchase

For a limited time, My Best Buy members (both new and existing, free to join) can receive a $50 promotional certificate when they preorder GTA 6 and purchase an eligible PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S console .

The deal is available to both new and existing My Best Buy members (free to join) , and applies to a wide range of consoles, including the PS5 Pro, PS5 Slim Digital Edition, PS5 Slim Disc Edition, Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, and even select refurbished PlayStation 5 models.

But, it is worth noting that eligible buyers won't receive their gift certificates immediately, and according to the retailer, will likely have to wait until around November 25, 2026, for it to appear in their My Best Buy account.

GTA 6: Should I Preorder a Physical or Digital Copy?

The obvious counterpoint to the idea of "physically owning" GTA 6 takes a bit of a hit when you remember there's no disc in the box, just a download code .

While this certainly isn't ideal , and definitely won't satify most physical media advocates, myself included, I can absolutely still see people wanting to own the box as a collector's item, a memento, or simply a marker of gaming history.

And there's no shame in that. Let's be honest, this is probably going to be the biggest game launch of all time. I'll be treating it as such, and you should too. (Still, it also would've been nice if they included a disc as well).

My second reason is a slightly more economic one. How sensible of me.

The global economy is a bit dicey right now (potentially understatement of the year, I know). Now, that's not going to stop millions of people buying GTA 6, but an $80 price tag is definitely enough to make at least some of us hesitate. At least, that's what Reddit commenters keep telling me, and they're famously the most intelligent among us.

For anyone who's not thrilled about paying $80 today for a digital copy, and then waiting several months to actually play the game (or simply doesn't have the cash available right now) a physical preorder through retailers like Amazon, Walmart, or Best Buy could make more sense.

Thanks to their preorder guarantees, these retailers won't charge you until your order ships . So if you're planning to spread the cost over the second half of the year, a physical preorder may actually be the smarter option.

Still, at the end of the day, this is entirely subjective. Just do whatever is best for you. Want to buy digitally? Go for it. Fancy a physical copy to delay the cost, or as a collector's item? Crack on!

GTA+ - 1-Month Free Included With Preorders

A digital preorder also gets you a free month of GTA+, with Rockstar referencing GTA Online:

"Experience the dynamic blockbuster GTA Online now with the best way to get the most out of its ever-evolving world. Pre-order any edition of Grand Theft Auto VI on the PlayStation Store or Microsoft Store and get one free month of GTA+ — featuring a recurring monthly GTA$500,000 deposit into your GTA Online character's bank account, access to special Shark Cards with 15% bonus GTA$, access to free and discounted GTA Online vehicles, a rotating selection of classic Rockstar Games titles and other featured games in the GTA+ Games Library, and much more."

It's worth noting that this auto-renews, so if you do redeem the free month of GTA+ - we'd advice turning that off at your nearest opportunity.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is set in Leonida , the GTA-universe version of Florida, where Vice City is located. Based on the trailers, it looks like you'll spend plenty of time in Vice City, but this isn't the 1980s version of the city from the 2002 game .

GTA 6 is set in the modern day, and the scope of the game expands well beyond the bounds of the urban area. In fact, it might represent the entire state. You'll visit the Leonida Keys, the Grassrivers marshland, Mount Kalaga National Park, among other locations .

The game centers on outlaws in love, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, who get roped into a wide-ranging criminal conspiracy. Much of what we know about the game comes from the trailers , which Rockstar has been oh-so gradually dropping onto the internet once a year since 2023.

On October 15, Rockstar released the official launch trailer for GTA 6 . It's an all-cinematic 90-second rundown of the game's story, accompanied by a banger of an original song called "Flower in a Hurricane," by the electronic duo Justice, featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & the Wizard Lizzard.

Rockstar released an "extended look" at GTA 6 on August 27. In an unusual move, it's streamed first on Netflix first, followed several hours later by its YouTube release.

The second GTA 6 trailer came out on May 6, 2025.

This trailer, set to The Pointer Sisters’ song “Hot Together,” zeroes in on protagonist Jason Duval as he goes about his day, doing house work, collecting rent checks for a relative, and picking up his girlfriend, Lucia Caminos, when she’s released from prison. They seem to have a healthy, loving relationship, but they can’t seem to stop doing crimes, Bonnie and Clyde-style.

According to the trailer’s description, “when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.“

Rockstar released the first trailer on December 4, 2023. Set to the Tom Petty song “Love Is a Long Road,” it shows off the Florida – er, Leonida – setting, with beaches, cities, and swamp areas. It also introduces the dual protagonists, Lucia and Jason.

Note that this trailer says the game is coming in 2025, but it was later delayed until May 2026 , and then, even later, delayed again to its current release date of November 19, 2026.

articles.title: The Skytech Ryzen X3D Edition Radeon RX 9070 XT Gaming PC With 32GB of RAM Drops to $1,999.99
articles.summary: Comfortably run games at up to 4K resolution without paying the Nvidia tax.
articles.body:
Walmart is offering a solid deal on a gaming PC that can run games in 4K. The Skytech Azure Gaming PC equipped with a Ryzen X3D CPU and Radeon RX 9070 XT GPU drops to $1,999.99 shipped after a $300 instant discount. The Radeon RX 9070 XT is a powerful GPU that nearly matches the performance of the now-$1,000+ GeForce RTX 5070 Ti.

Skytech Ryzen X3D Edition Radeon RX 9070 XT PC for $1,999.99

Skytech Azure AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D Radeon RX 9070 XT Gaming PC (32GB/1TB)

The Skytech Azure is equipped with an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D CPU, Radeon RX 9070 XT GPU, 32GB of DDR5-5600MHz RAM, and a 1TB PCIe 4 M.2 SSD. The CPU is cooled by a 360mm liquid AIO and the system is powered by an 850W 80Plus Gold certified power supply that offers extra headroom for future upgrades.

The AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D is still one of the best gaming CPUs

Although it has been succeeded by the newer 9000X3D series of processors, the AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D maintains its reputation of being one of the best gaming CPUs you can get right now. According to Passmark , the 7800X3D's gaming performance surpasses that of the newer Intel Core Ultra 7 265K. The 7800X3D also consumes less power and produces less heat than the 9800X3D while maintaining nearly the same gaming performance.

The Radeon RX 9070 XT Received a 10/10 at IGN

The AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT is the only 2025-released GPU that we gave a 10/10 score . This is the least expensive graphics card from either AMD or Nvidia that I would comfortably recommend for playing the latest and most demanding games in 4K at 60fps or higher. Even though it costs about $400 less than the Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti in today's market, the 9070 XT matches it or beats in several of the games we tested. The RTX 5070 Ti does pull away when you factor in DLSS or ray tracing, but if you want those technologies you'll have to pay dearly for them.

articles.title: Zangief Actor Olivier Richters Really Wants to Play Tyr in the Live-Action God of War Show
articles.summary: We got the chance to chat with Olivier Richters on the Street Fighter red carpet, who told us that he would love to play Tyr in Prime Video’s live-action God of War series.
articles.body:
We got the chance to chat with Olivier Richters on the Street Fighter red carpet, who told us that he would love to play Tyr in Prime Video’s live-action God of War series.

Richters is a massive man. Standing over seven feet tall and weighing more than 350 pounds, it makes sense why he was cast as Zangief in the Street Fighter movie — and it’s also the reason why he wants to try his hand at playing Tyr.

In fact, he credits it for being the reason why he didn’t make the cut to play Kratos when Ryan Hurst, who was previously cast in the role, was forced to leave the project after sustaining a serious bicep injury while filming a stunt for the show.

“I think I can be open [about it],” he told us. “I did an audition. I really got high up the chain, even got two callbacks, and eventually they chose Dave Bautista . Much respect for him, he’s a great choice. Of course, in some universe if he didn’t exist, I would have loved to play the role. Maybe in the future.

“Every year I’m acting, I’m learning more and more. If I’m really honest, I think there’s one character who suits me better, and that’s Tyr. I would love to play him. I don’t know if he’s gonna be portrayed in the first season or second season, but my agent told them, ‘Olivier wants to be Tyr.’ So, let’s see if it happens.”

Richters mentioned this back in February on his Instagram account, showing himself decked out in a Kratos cosplay. “Realistically... at 7'2" / 2.18m, I might be too big for the role. I would literally tower over every other character. My real dream? A chance to audition for Týr. That would, in my opinion, be perfect,” he wrote.

While his future in the God of War show is currently unclear, he’s now reveling in the spotlight as Zangief in the new Street Fighter movie. In fact, he’s training in Street Fighter 6 right now with some seasoned pros with genuine hopes to be the “best” Zangief on all fronts — not just in the movies.

“I’m not lying — I’m really dedicated to becoming one of the best Zangiefs out there,” he revealed. “I’m not there yet, but I want to enter a tournament one time as the real Zangief playing Zangief. I just met a pro Zangief player, we spoke, and we’re gonna train together. If there is gonna be a second [movie], I want to be the ultimate Zangief.”

As a member of the fighting game community, I can definitely say that we welcome Richters into the fold with open arms and can’t wait to see him at a major someday. Maybe Evo 2027?

articles.title: Valve May Be Working on an OLED Steam Frame, According to Datamined Source Code
articles.summary: The Steam Frame came out a month ago, and while it is one of the best PCVR headsets, its lenses weren't quite as high-quality as some of its competitors. However, it seems like Valve might be working on a mid-generation refresh with OLED optics.
articles.body:
The Steam Frame came out a month ago, and while it's one of the best PCVR headsets out there, its lenses weren't quite as high-quality as some of its competitors. However, it seems like Valve might be working on a mid-generation refresh with OLED optics.

According to SteamFrameHub , which dug through some of the source code for the Steam Frame kernel, the OS has references to a different Steam Frame with OLED optics, code named 'Plano.' Take this with a massive grain of salt, of course. But if it's real, the Plano headset would have largely the same specs as the existing Steam Frame, just with OLED panels with a per-eye resolution of 3,552x3,840, compared to the 2,160x2,160 pancake lenses found in the Steam Frame.

A higher-resolution OLED display would do wonders for the Steam Frame, especially for anyone using it for PCVR, rather than trying to play standalone games. Those better lenses would come a much higher price, though; as SteamFrameHub notes, the leaked optic specs line up nicely with the lenses found in the Samsung Galaxy XR headset, which starts for around $1,799. However, that headset launched before the RAM crisis kicked off, so a Steam Frame that matched its specs would likely be at least a bit more expensive.

Just like the rest of Valve's hardware this year, the Steam Frame was supposed to kick off a new era of accessible PC hardware, fueled by SteamOS at its center. However, because of an ongoing RAM crisis that won't be ending any time soon, the impact has been greatly diminished. Still, there are at least some people who seem to be buying the Steam Frame and the Steam Machine, as they're both still completely sold out at the time of writing.

Because Valve is still working on getting through the reservation list and waitlist for the Steam Fame, it's safe to assume that even if a Steam Frame OLED is a thing that will actually exist, it probably won't come out for quite a long time. The real question then, is whether or not that'll happen before Valve finds the perfect chipset that'll make the company want to make a Steam Deck 2 . Just like with everything else Valve, we'll simply have to wait and see.

articles.title: Xbox Reportedly Surveys Users On Return to Full Exclusivity for its Games
articles.summary: Xbox has reportedly surveyed players on how they would feel about a return to console exclusivity for all of its games, with the exception of Call of Duty.
articles.body:
Xbox has reportedly surveyed players on how they would feel about a return to console exclusivity for all of its games, with the exception of Call of Duty.

The survey, first spotted and shared by Windows Central , asks fans multiple questions about exclusivity. Some of these questions ask about specific games, such as Fallout, being exclusive to Xbox consoles and PC, while one question asks fans to imagine a world where all Xbox titles, excluding Call of Duty, were made exclusive to Xbox and PC. Interestingly, one question also suggests removing Minecraft from sale on platforms like PlayStation and Nintendo, though players who already own the game could keep it. However, existing Minecraft games would not receive any further updates.

"Imagine it was announced that all future title releases from every Xbox-developed gaming franchise except Call of Duty will be console-exclusive to Xbox," the question reads. "For Minecraft only, existing titles would no longer be available for purchase on PlayStation or Nintendo consoles, and would not receive any new content updates. However, there is no impact to any of the existing titles or content you already own. Nothing changes on PC in this announcement."

The survey's questions are largely trying to see if fans really care about exclusivity, if they would switch hardware for it, or if they would skip a game because it was made exclusive. Whether this will actually amount to anything remains to be seen; companies consider a wide range of possibilities, regardless of how realistic they may be. However, all of this suggests that Xbox is at least considering on doubling down on exclusivity.

Earlier this summer, Xbox announced that Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution would be exclusive to Xbox and PC forever , but were hesitant to confirm exclusivity for other titles. Games like Forza Horizon 6 and Fable are still slated to come to PS5 , but it's unclear what will happen when something major like The Elder Scrolls 6 is released.

As of right now, we'll just have to wait and see what the future holds. Xbox is in a pretty critical spot right now, where it is trying desperately to salvage not only its reputation, but its financial viability after a tough generation. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly pointed the finger at Game Pass in a recent meeting , as players were no longer incentivized to purchase major releases like Call of Duty on day one.

Xbox has spent this year walking back some of its previous plans by pulling Call of Duty from Game Pass on day one, and it's also rumored to be making some changes to day one offerings in 2027 . It'll be interesting to see where Sharma takes Xbox next, but it does appear that they're trying to see what fans want before making some big changes.

articles.title: Lanterns Season 2 Isn't a Guarantee, But a Decision Will Be Made This Year
articles.summary: Lanterns Season 2 isn't a guarantee, but DC boss Peter Safran says they will decide by the end of the year whether it moves forward.
articles.body:
Lanterns Season 2 isn't a guarantee, but DC boss Peter Safran says a decision will be made as to whether or not it moves forward by the end of 2026.

Speaking with IGN, Safran confirmed that there is a writer's room currently hashing out ideas for the future of Lanterns right now, but it will all depend on whether or not they come up with a good enough story worthy of following up the first season. He noted that TV is an important part of DC's future, but that they're waiting to see if there's a story worth telling before giving the greenlight to Lanterns Season 2.

"The episodic world is always going to be a really important part of our overall slate, it's a great way to tell stories that need more real estate than a feature film can offer you, and it's a great way to introduce characters that we then bring into the feature world," said Safran. "And I think that Aaron Pierre and John Stewart are a perfect example of that. We introduced him in Lanterns, and audiences will see him next summer in Man of Tomorrow. So, it's really important to us in continuing to tell aspects of the story that we're not telling in the feature film world, so there's more to come.

"Listen, we'll see what happens with Lanterns Season 2. If, I think, the collective group of HBO and DC and Chris Mundy and the team all feel like we've got something that is a worthy successor to quite a beloved first season of television, then I wouldn't be surprised to see more."

Safran confirmed to Collider that it would have a decision on whether Lanterns Season 2 moves forward by the end of the year.

As Safran noted, John Stewart or the Lantern Corps will not suddenly cease to exist in the DCU if Season 2 doesn't move forward. John Stewart is already confirmed to appear in Man of Tomorrow , the sequel to James Gunn's Superman. Fans are also hoping that Hal Jordan will return, but... well, we'll just have to see what the future holds at this point.

Lanterns Season 1 certainly leaves the door open for more stories around Stewart and potentially Jordan, if the writers and showrunners play their cards right. The series is also one of HBO's most successful shows of the year, so it seems hard to imagine that the powers that be aren't hungry for another season of this show.

Lanterns managed to succeed due to its two charming leads, more mature tone, and compelling mystery. It successfully aped the style of True Detective while making itself feel unique in the extremely saturated comic book genre. Just two months before Lanterns' premiere, Supergirl bombed at the box office, and some fans began to fear the DCU was already in trouble. The success of Lanterns seems to disprove that idea .

Whether the show returns remains to be seen, but you can expect fans to have their pitchforks ready if DC and Warner Bros. don't give it the greenlight.

articles.title: DC Studios Co-Boss Peter Safran Reaffirms Franchise Slate After Skydance Acquisition
articles.summary: IGN spoke with DC Studios’ co-CEO and co-chairman Peter Safran this week about the status of the studio’s future projects now that Warner Bros. has been acquired by Skydance. Our discussion ranged from Clayface to their upcoming feature film, television and animated projects.
articles.body:
I spoke with DC Studios’ co-CEO and co-chairman Peter Safran this week about the status of the studio’s future projects now that Warner Bros. has been acquired by Skydance .

Our discussion ranged from DC’s newest release, Clayface , to their upcoming feature film, television and animated projects, including The Batman: Part Two , Man of Tomorrow , The People v. Gorilla Grodd , Mister Miracle , and what DC Studios co-boss and filmmaker James Gunn might direct after his Superman follow-up.

My chat with Peter Safran follows. It has been edited for clarity.

IGN: Congratulations on Clayface actually happening. Back in the day, the best we could have hoped for is a SyFy Channel movie. Like Man-Thing .

Peter Safran: Exactly, exactly. Well, thankfully, we all did grow up loving “ Feat of Clay" in the [Batman] animated series so, when [Mike] Flanagan came in to pitch us , he had a very, very receptive audience, that is for sure.

So, we've had a few things but it's only the third narrative feature to come out, which is probably not what one would necessarily expect when you're rebooting a whole universe. But we've always said that we're going to be driven by good screenplays, and Flanagan wrote a great screenplay.

IGN: Clayface is going to be the first release under the new Skydance regime. I know you have to be circumspect about private conversations, but were you and James given any marching orders from David Ellison about what maybe he'd like to see from the DCU going forward?

Peter Safran: You know what, he was very complimentary about what we've done and just wants to give us the resources to keep doing what we're doing. I think he sees the long-term vision that we have and we certainly laid it out for him earlier this year, and he wants us to keep doing that.

IGN: Clayface is the smallest movie you guys have done. I like that it's basically the movie that doesn't get made much anymore, $40 million or whatever movie. Do you plan on making some more of these smaller films or is it a wait and see kind of thing?

Peter Safran: We've always said that our slate should have a very broad spectrum of tones and budgets and scales and scopes and this is just another example of us living up to what we said we were going to do. James and I are both pretty, and you and I have talked about horror for years, James and I are very steeped in the world of horror so the fact that we can make a full on R-rated body horror picture but under the banner of DCU and within the DCU is incredibly exciting, that's really a dream come true. And at its core, Clayface for us really represents exactly the creative flexibility that makes DC unique.

So, from its conception, the project was never designed to be a traditional superhero movie, but it was always a character-driven story that uses DC mythology to explore obsession, identity, fame, transformation, to explore those themes. So, it really does represent the kind of thing that we were talking about early on, and I think that audiences really do crave things that feel different and this one truly does.

I think that the genre approach, rather than following the conventions of a classic comic book spectacle, instead we're, and you saw the movie last night, we're leaning into the psychological body horror elements creating this really unsettling experience. And the character's ability to physically transform becomes a vehicle to explore these deeper human fears about identity and self-worth and losing control and there's a real story at its heart, there's a real character journey at the heart of this movie. And I always say that the best horror movie is, if you strip out the horror, there's still a good drama and I feel like that's what this is. It's got some real depth to it. I think people are going to be surprised when they see it and I think that that point of differentiation that you've never seen a comic book adaptation in the film world like this is something that audiences are going to grasp onto.

IGN: Clayface is set in Gotham City. James has said it's in the DCU. How much of that should the fans actually take to heart? Will this be what Gotham City is going to look like when you finally make Batman: The Brave and the Bold ?

Peter Safran: What we've always said is that there's a consistency to the look but the next filmmaker that tackles Gotham, they [can] use it as a starting point, they can all feel different. I think each filmmaker, just the way great comic book creators treat stories differently within the same worlds and with the same characters in the comic books, we want each film to have its own reflection of the vision of the filmmaker. Listen, Gotham is a grittier, dirtier place, for example, than Coast City and I don't think, suddenly, Gotham's not going to become Paris, and so I think that that's always going to be consistent.

But I think, actually, [Clayface director James] Watkins did a really good job layering in the darker, grittier feel, but with also a slight glimpse like when you're inside his apartment before he gets turfed out of it. But you get a little bit of sense of what money can buy you in Gotham, there's an elegance to it as well, a Beaux-Arts brilliance to it that can exist but we all know that Gotham is a little dirty, is a little gritty, is a little dangerous.

IGN: Now that Lanterns has wrapped up Season One , what is the plan for DC on television at this point?

Peter Safran: Well, we're obviously in production on Gorilla Grodd right now, we have a number of other properties that we're really excited about that we're in development on. The episodic world is always going to be a really important part of our overall slate. It's a great way to tell stories that need more real estate than a feature film can offer you, and it's a great way to introduce characters that we then bring into the feature world. And I think that Aaron Pierre and John Stewart are perfect examples of that. We introduced him in Lanterns and audiences will see him next summer in Man of Tomorrow. So, it's really important to us in continuing to tell aspects of the story that we're not telling in the feature film world so there's more to come.

Listen, we'll see what happens with Lanterns Season Two . If, I think, the collective group of HBO and DC and Chris Mundy and the team all feel like we've got something that is a worthy successor to quite a beloved first season of television, then I wouldn't be surprised to see more.

IGN: But Lanterns Season Two is not green lit?

IGN: What project do you think will be the next after Gorilla Grodd to go before cameras?

Peter Safran: There are a couple that are vying for that spot, but we haven't firmly committed to what the next one will be in either film or television. We have a pretty robust slate of animation that's all going forward right now but, on the live-action side, it's a little bit TBD.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

IGN: Obviously, just from a marketplace perspective, you don't want to have dueling Batmans out there.

Peter Safran: No. Listen, we know that we've got Batman: Part Two and [the animated film] Dynamic Duo in 2028. Listen, I couldn't be more excited about the plans that we have over the next five years and, obviously, a lot of them, we're just not able to talk about yet, but I think you're never going to please everybody, but I have a feeling that people are going to be excited about what we have coming up. And, again, Batman: Part Two, everybody's aware of the issues we're having right now , but, what we've seen so far of the shoot, it looked absolutely fantastic and Matt Reeves is a supremely talented filmmaker. Dynamic Duo is, for my money, as original today as Pixar was when they did Toy Story so we're really excited about that. Obviously, Man of Tomorrow's in post [production] right now.

IGN: On that television front, you did announce some interesting animated projects at the Annecy festival . What can you tell us about where some of those are right now?

Peter Safran: Somewhere in early stages. Absolute Batman , (Scott Snyder’s) just working on the scripts right now. Mr. Miracle, I think that Tom King really learned a lot in his season of co-creating and executive producing Lanterns and he adapted his book Mr. Miracle fully on his own, wrote all eight episodes and I think it's just dynamite. Josh Hutcherson as Scott Free and Mackenzie Davis as Big Barda. And I just think it's a book that I've always loved and I remember Tom telling us early on that, every convention he goes to, at least a couple people come up to him and say this book saved my life and I love that we got to tell that story over eight episodes. And it's just a beautiful story about, “How do we survive in today's world knowing that we're never going to truly know the answers to the big questions in life?” It's a beautiful book and the adaptation is fantastic so we're excited about that.

IGN: And that Joker anime sounds really interesting.

Peter Safran: Yeah, that's one of the earlier phases of development, working on the scripts right now. The ones that are really advanced are Creature Commandos Season Two, Mr. Miracle, My Adventures with Green Lantern, Starfire and DC Superpowers. Those are all creatively way down the road. So, we're really excited because we love animation, we love the art form and the fact that we're going to have such a robust slate coming out is fantastic.

IGN: When do you think the marketing push and reveals will start happening for Man of Tomorrow?

Peter Safran: I think it's early days, it's early days. That's something that we'll determine in the coming month.

IGN: Has David Ellison mentioned at all any ideas or changes in how to market the DC movies or no?

Peter Safran: No, not yet. But, remember, the whole thing's a week old, it was literally last Tuesday.

Peter Safran: Yeah, it's early days. But it's a coming home for us with [theatrical marketing and distribution executive] Josh Goldstine though to have him back involved in our movies as head of marketing and distribution and he's terrific, super smart and we've got a great relationship with him. So, I think that everything's to be discussed as we move forward. But, listen, they're already jumping in on Clayface, everybody's excited about that release and so it's great to be able to talk to Josh again about our business.

IGN: Has James Gunn decided the next movie he's going to direct yet?

IGN: He could probably use a bit of a breather, I suppose.

Peter Safran: He really loves what he does. There was that time where he was writing the full season of Creature Commandos and writing and directing Peacemaker Season Two and prepping the first Superman movie . So, he's got a never-ending enthusiasm and excitement for what we're building so I wouldn't expect him to take too much time in between Man of Tomorrow and whatever he does next.

IGN: I want to be very delicate about how I ask this. Is there any scenario where Batman: Part Two doesn't start filming again?

articles.title: Marvel TV Boss Says Daredevil: Born Again Was Always Meant to End With Season 3, Despite Previously Suggesting Otherwise
articles.summary: Head of Marvel Television Brad Winderbaum says Daredevil: Born Again was always planned to end with Season 3, despite previously suggesting otherwise.
articles.body:
Head of Marvel Television Brad Winderbaum says Daredevil: Born Again was always planned to end with Season 3, despite previously suggesting otherwise.

In a new interview with The Brandon Davis Show , Winderbaum was asked about Season 3 being the end of the show. He noted that the plan was "always to culminate at [Season] 3," despite the news of the show ending coming as a surprise to fans .

“The plan was always to culminate at 3, because the way we’re looking at it, the original [Netflix] series is 3 seasons, Born Again is 3 seasons. They’re kind of like trade paperbacks or collections that you can slot into your shelves, like these are two 3-volume sets, and then we will take a breath and figure out what’s next for the character.”

Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 Set Photos

Actor Charlie Cox also suggested the same thing at New York Comic-Con, telling GamesRadar that there was a "bit more planning and emotional support" this time. The original Netflix series was unexpectedly and unceremoniously canceled, much to the surprise of the show's writers and cast. However, at some point, the actors were told Born Again would serve as the finale.

Interestingly, Winderbaum told Screen Rant in 2025 that the show was meant to be annualized, with a new season dropping every March.

"That is the plan," said Winderbaum ahead of Season 1 of Born Again. "Season 2 will come out next year, and then hopefully Season 3 and Season Infinity after that. I think this world is extremely rich, and there are many stories to be told on the streets of New York."

Of course, plans may have changed if Disney and Marvel realized the viewership wasn't there. It sounds like, at the very least, the show didn't abruptly have the plug pulled after filming wrapped on Season 3. Even if the show ending with Season 3 wasn't the plan from the very beginning of Born Again's run, it may have shifted in that direction during the development and writing of the third season. Whether Daredevil will return in a future MCU project remains to be seen, but fans still want to see the Man Without Fear team up with Spidey. Cox himself is uncertain of Daredevil's future, but has urged fans to campaign to bring the character back .

"Don't know, man. I don't know," he said when asked whether or not he's done as Daredevil. "I mean, it might be. It might be. Don't worry about Kevin [Feige]. Get the Save Daredevil campaign on the horn. Get them motivated. That engine, that won't stop until there's some resolution. That's my true superpower, is the Save Daredevil campaign!"

articles.title: Obsession Star Inde Navarrette Says She Studied Anime Like Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer to Learn Screenwriting
articles.summary: Inde Navarrette, best known for her role as Nikki Freeman in Obsession, says she took a deep dive into anime to better understand screenwriting and storytelling.
articles.body:
Inde Navarrette, best known for her role as Nikki Freeman in Obsession, says she took a deep dive into anime to better understand screenwriting and storytelling while waiting for her star to rise.

Navarrette’s breakout role as Nikki in Obsession didn’t skyrocket her to stardom overnight. In fact, there was a time between the film's completion and its eventual release when she wasn’t sure what was next for her career.

During that period, she began to stream games on Twitch to make ends meet, and even started studying storytelling in film and TV by watching some of her favorite anime series — specifically, Demon Slayer and Jujutsu Kaisen .

“I transitioned into studying film and watching movies and asking, ‘Why do I like them?’” she said in an October 14 interview with The Hollywood Reporter. “What I like is anime, so like, why do I like that? I mean, Jujutsu Kaisen I find to be a very fascinating anime, but why is it so different than Demon Slayer? Why is it so different than other ones? With Jujutsu Kaisen, they play with timelines, right? With Demon Slayer, they don’t, it’s very linear. And what does that mean and how does that affect with storytelling?

“I really dove into, ‘Why is Jujutsu Kaisen so good?’ And I learned about timeline and about storytelling — how a person can have a monologue at the beginning of the episode that matters two episodes later or even at the end, and that person’s dead and you don’t learn it until then — and then attaching that to my screenwriting and trying to learn that way.”

Navarrette is a self-proclaimed nerd; on top of loving anime, she’s also a huge gamer, as evidenced by her (now scrubbed clean) Twitch channel. She was elated when a fan gave her a sealed 2009 copy of Modern Warfare 2 still in its display case back in July at a fan convention, too.

She’s even branching into voice acting, saying one of her dream projects is to voice a character in a Resident Evil game . “I wanna try something smaller to kind of test the waters, and then later, [do something] different, because video games are obviously a big interest of mine,” she said in an August interview. “I love that world, specifically — the Resident Evil world.”

For now, Navarrette is gearing up to play Rogue in Marvel Studios’ X-Men reboot , which she’s assured fans that she’s doing everything in her power to pull off successfully.

"I'm doing everything humanly possible because I love that character," Navarrette said . "I've studied that character. I want to do it justice for myself, for [director Jake Schrieier], for what they want to portray and also for what I as a fan want her to be like. I’m doing everything, exclamation point."

Given that she’s making a point to start voice acting, it opens up the possibility that maybe someday we’ll hear her in an English dub someday... maybe in a future season of Jujutsu Kaisen?

articles.title: Brewers on the verge of dethroning the Dodgers after wild NLCS Game 3 win
articles.summary: Heading into Game 3 of the NLCS, the Los Angeles Dodgers had everything to prove against the Milwaukee Brewers. With the chance at the elusive three-peat on...
articles.body:
Heading into Game 3 of the NLCS, the Los Angeles Dodgers had everything to prove against the Milwaukee Brewers.

With the chance at the elusive three-peat on the line and a pair of losses already on the books from their time in Milwaukee, the Dodgers wanted to prove they still deserved the title of World Series favorite, but instead, they simply came up short, with errors on the field and in the dugout resulting in a brutal 6-2 loss to the Brewers.

After allowing a shocking home run on the very first pitch of the game, Blake Snell was a dominant force for Los Angeles, recording nine strikeouts through six innings. But after watching his team take the lead in the bottom of the sixth, going up 2-1 by playing Brewers-style baseball, disaster struck when Jake Bauers turned a double-digit pitch at-bat into a 3-2 lead, with Garrett Mitchell somehow smashing another bomb on the very next pitch after Dave Roberts somehow didn't go to his bullpen.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

From there, the game largely went away from the Dodgers, almost by design. After Evan Phillips closed out the seventh with just one hit and Roki Sasaki took care of just one batter before being replaced by Justin Wrobleski in the eighth, who closed out the final 1.2 while giving up another run on an errant throw.

No Tanner Scott. No Edwin Diaz. Just a former starting pitcher who wasn't even on the NLDS roster after a tough end to the regular season.

Will the Dodgers be able to keep the series alive in Game 4? Maybe yes, maybe no, but down 3-0 with the potential go-home contest scheduled for Thursday at 5 PM PT, fans won't have to wait long to find out.

articles.title: Brewers stun Dodgers with back-to-back homers in 7th inning and take 3-0 lead in NLCS with 6-2 win
articles.summary: Los Angeles had just taken a 2-1 lead in the sixth before getting stunned. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elim...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell as Milwaukee regained the lead in the seventh inning, and the Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to take a 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series.

Los Angeles had just taken a 2-1 lead in the sixth before getting stunned. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination.

"All three games we've played so far, and hopefully that continues, where just every time they score, we come back and score," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "That's not easy to do in baseball."

Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium, where the Brewers can become the first major league club to complete a postseason sweep after getting swept by that same opponent in the previous postseason. Los Angeles took all four games against Milwaukee in the NLCS last year.

The only other time the Dodgers trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.

The lone team in big league history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven postseason series was the Boston Red Sox in the 2004 AL Championship Series against the New York Yankees.

"We've won four in a row a number of times this year," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "We've got to win tomorrow. That's our only focus."

Coming into the seventh, Snell had retired 14 batters in a row. The first pitch of the game thrown by the two-time Cy Young Award winner was hit for a home run by Jackson Chourio, and his last pitch was Mitchell's solo shot.

Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the inning and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412-foot drive to right field on the 11th pitch of the at-bat for a 3-2 lead as most of the players in Milwaukee's dugout came onto the field to celebrate.

Mitchell was next and his drive traveled 428 feet to right-center. That chased Snell, who hadn't given up a home run in 46 1/3 innings this year entering the game. It was only the second time in his career the left-hander served up multiple home runs to left-handed hitters in one game.

And it was the latest relentless plate appearance for Bauers, who drew a 12-pitch walk from Yoshinobu Yamamoto that helped the Brewers go ahead early in Game 2.

Milwaukee, which has never beaten the Dodgers in three previous playoff series, is chasing its second pennant and first in the National League. The Brewers were in the American League when they reached their only World Series, a seven-game loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982.

Snell gave up four runs and four hits in six innings, struck out nine and walked two.

The Brewers extended the lead to 5-2 in the eighth on Justin Wrobleski's wild pitch that scored Brice Turang, who reached on an infield single and advanced to third on William Contreras' single. They added another run on Joey Ortiz's two-strike RBI single in the ninth.

The offensively starved Dodgers took their first lead, 2-1, on Will Smith's two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth.

After rookie starter Robert Gasser pitched five shutout innings, Uribe entered and loaded the bases on walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who was 1 for 25 in the playoffs, doubled off the left-center fence with one out for his first hit of the NLCS.

DL Hall took over from Uribe and stranded runners at second and third by striking out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman.

Hall allowed one hit in 2 1/3 scoreless innings to improve to 3-0 in these playoffs. Trevor Megill got four outs for his second save of the series and fourth this postseason.

The Dodgers played from behind again after the 22-year-old Chourio connected for his third career leadoff homer as fans were still heading to their seats.

After that, Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 in a row — six on strikeouts — before getting hammered in the seventh.

The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings, but couldn't get enough across. They have yet to homer in the NLCS.

Ohtani was 1 for 2 with a walk while hitting sixth in the order, the lowest he's batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago.

articles.title: DC’s Mister Miracle Animated Series Lead Voices Confirmed
articles.summary: DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran reveals the voices behind Scott Free and Big Barda.
articles.body:
DC’s upcoming animated series Mister Miracle will star Josh Hutcherson (The Hunger Games, Five Nights at Freddy’s) as Scott Free and Mackenzie Davis (Speak No Evil, Terminator: Dark Fate) as Big Barda. The news comes via DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran himself, speaking with IGN in an interview published earlier today.

Safran also noted showrunner Tom King has written all eight episodes of the series himself. King, a prolific DC author, created the 12-issue, Eisner Award-winning 2017 Mister Miracle series alongside artist Mitch Gerads. That comic forms the basis for this upcoming animated series.

“I think that Tom King really learned a lot in his season of co-creating and executive producing Lanterns and he adapted his book Mister Miracle fully on his own, wrote all eight episodes and I think it’s just dynamite,” said Safran. “Josh Hutcherson as Scott Free and Mackenzie Davis as Big Barda. And I just think it’s a book that I’ve always loved and I remember Tom telling us early on that, every convention he goes to, at least a couple people come up to him and say this book saved my life and I love that we got to tell that story over eight episodes.”

A network or arrival date for Mister Miracle is yet to be discussed.

For its part, it’s not yet confirmed whether Lanterns is a lock for a second season, but Safran confirmed that a potential future for that series is currently being hashed out, depending on whether they can find a story worthy of following up the first season.

articles.title: How The Diplomat Season 4 Turns an Assassination Attempt and Marital Drama Into the Best Political Thriller Currently on Television
articles.summary: Netflix's The Diplomat Season 4 has standout performances from Keri Russell and Allison Janney that elevate the series into the best political thriller on TV.
articles.body:
Spoilers below for Season 4 of Netflix’s The Diplomat . All episodes are streaming now.

At its core, Season 4 of The Diplomat is a series of one-on-one conversations in which the fate of the world hangs in the balance. The president and vice president, first gentleman and chief of staff, prime ministers, ambassadors, and domestic workers all engage in rich, dramatic dialogue that immediately sucks you in and doesn’t loosen its grip until the season cuts to black. Tight closeups, thick tension, and carefully constructed language imbued with double, triple, and sometimes quadruple meanings unfurl in scene after scene, creating a tapestry of geopolitical and domestic conflict that’s hard to turn away from.

The Netflix series follows American Ambassador to the United Kingdom Kate Wyler (Keri Russell) as she walks the tightrope of managing a simmering international conflict while attempting to save her marriage to her husband, Hal (Rufus Sewell). In Season 4, The Diplomat continues to be a crackling, pulpy thriller with superb writing, gorgeous cinematography, and top-tier performances.

With a new batch of episodes, the show brings what was an already fraught series of storylines to a furious boil. In the aftermath of discovering that President Grace Penn (Allison Janney) colluded with Hal (promoted to vice president in Season 3 ) to steal an “apocalypse weapon” from a Russian submarine, Kate launches into a campaign of dealmaking and double-crossing to try to get the situation under control. As the season begins, we’re led to believe that the conspiracy will be the central conflict for the foreseeable future. But all of that is quickly scuttled by a harrowing assasination attempt on the president.

The scene, which closes out the premiere episode, is one of the most realistic acts of fictional political violence ever filmed. There’s no music, no building tension; just two quick pops and a shirt suddenly soaked with blood. It's indicative of what The Diplomat does best: presenting the extraordinary as subtle and restrained while still underscoring the global stakes.

This ethos is especially apparent in the still beautifully dysfunctional relationship between Kate and Hal. As the world burns and nuclear conflict is only an itchy trigger finger away, Kate and Hal’s marriage is the spine on which everything else in The Diplomat rests. They’re at once warm with each other yet blisteringly cold, trusting and incredibly suspicious, totally in love but always on the verge of mutually assured destruction. Sewell and Russell continue to be dynamite, layering their scenes together with half-truths, knowing glances, and winking humor. Their on-screen chemistry bursting with intelligence and desire, Hal and Kate often can’t stand each other but would wither away without the other’s counsel.

While Seasons 1-3 of The Diplomat focused mostly on Kate and Hal’s relationship, Season 4 ups Janney’s President Grace Penn and Bradley Whitford’s hilarious but secretly ruthless first gentleman Todd to near co-lead status. Their relationship seethes with a familiarity colored by a brutal imbalance of power. Whitford, in particular, takes full advantage of the show’s darkly comedic writing, imbuing his character with an “aw shucks” brand of humor that belies a knack for cunningly eviscerating anyone who stands between him and his wife. A post-assassination attempt conversation early in the season in which Todd dresses down White House Chief of Staff Billie Appiah (Nana Mensah) is one of those two-handers that highlights the show’s tour de force storytelling and brilliant acting.

As the president, Janney has never been better. Intricately drawn and perfectly performed, Grace Penn is a revelation of a character. Her steeliness and win-at-all-costs attitude of Seasons 2–3 is still intact, but these traits are now forged with a twinge of uncertainty and a whole lot of post-shooting PTSD. As Penn, Janney is at once flighty and megalomaniacal, grounded and borderline mad, caring and absolutely unforgiving. The character knows the consequences of her actions, yet still hasn’t found a line she will not cross. Grace Penn is the most complex, well-drawn president ever put on screen and Janney hits a grand slam in every scene she’s in.

While the four core characters drive much of the show’s drama, The Diplomat features a stacked cast of supporting players who fill out the show’s beautifully crafted world. Ali Ahn and Ato Essandoh shine as Kate’s embassy colleagues Eidra and Stuart. Their budding romance is a twisted mirror of the show’s two other central couples, showing what happens when a relationship heats up after you’re already colleagues instead of vice versa. Rory Kinnear once again chews the scenery to bits as Prime Minister Nicol Trowbridge, especially in a mid-season episode where he’s given a series of fantasy sequences leading up to his blackmail-induced resignation. Doctor Who’s Jodie Whittaker appears late in the season as the new PM, calmly igniting a whole new set of problems for the U.S. government.

Four seasons into The Diplomat, the show’s writing is still obscenely good. Showrunner Debora Cahn and her team of writers synthesize conflicts both personal and global, sprinkle them with a bit of realistic humor, and continually paint the mythological figures at the center of the show as real people.

A scene in the premiere episode shows Kate following the president of the United States into a ladies’ room to press her on an important issue. A storyline, in which Todd (who finagles his way into a London-based job) suspects Kate of being pregnant, unfolds in a way unique to virtually any fictional half-baked pregnancy scenario you can imagine. An international cover-up hinges on whether a team of bureaucrats can convince another team of bureaucrats that they are bad at math. A climactic scene between Grace, Todd, Kate, and Hal that's straight out of Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? is interrupted by an overeager chef. Cahn’s roots in The West Wing are on full display here. But whereas that show hinged on optimism, The Diplomat subverts that feel-good mentality for realism that’s far more brutal but no less entertaining.

The rest of The Diplomat fires on all cylinders throughout Season 4. Characters walk-and-talk through castle after gorgeous castle. The scenery and cinematography are moody and rich. A late season sojourn to Italy for the G7 summit allows the crew to pull off a series of unbroken long takes that would make David Fincher proud. All of this blends into a spellbinding series of episodes that are pulpy, hilarious, heartbreaking, and downright shocking.

Some of the plot machinations in The Diplomat still can be a bit far-fetched; the show still strains to invent reasons why American government officials need to constantly travel to the UK and some realism is forsaken for the sake of jaw-dropping drama. A few plotlines are even ripped right from the lesser seasons of House of Cards. And yet, it’s still a whip-smart commentary on international politics as they are now. The show forces its audience to reckon with the undeniable truth that the people who run the world are human beings prone to pettiness, stubbornness, and loneliness, and that those qualities often spill over into life-altering decisions for everyone else.

The Diplomat is truly a show for our times, showing how intense, messy relationships — often no more profound than two people talking in a room — can upend lives, transform the mundane into the extraordinary, and have serious consequences for the world at large.

articles.title: Police arrest US teen in alleged Illinois Hindu temple mass shooting plot
articles.summary: Coworker alerted police after receiving disturbing messages from 19-year-old suspect.
articles.body:
A ‌teenager arrested in a Chicago suburb had shared a document expressing ⁠white supremacist ⁠views and outlined an alleged plan to carry out a mass shooting, potentially targeting a Hindu place of worship, police in the US state of Illinois have said.

Alexandros Paporakis, 19, of Palatine, was arrested on Sunday after an individual reported receiving concerning electronic communications from him, Palatine police said on Wednesday. It was not ⁠immediately clear whether he had legal representation.

Detectives searched Paporakis’s home and recovered a rifle, multiple loaded rifle magazines and hundreds of additional rounds of rifle ammunition.

“Among the recovered items was a tactical vest containing body armor and a patch displaying imagery associated with white supremacist extremism,” a police statement said.

Paporakis’s coworker reportedly told police that he openly identified himself as a white supremacist at work and said he “couldn’t wait” to kill Indian people, according to prosecutors from the Cook County State’s Attorney’s office.

Detectives recovered a document called “Why I fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter’s Manifesto)” which had sentiments expressing white supremacist and extremist ideologies, referencing violence towards South Asians, specifically Indians.

Authorities believed Paporakis was planning to carry out his attack on Sunday, possibly targeting a Hindu temple in Aurora, 40 miles (65km) southwest of Palatine.

“However, the specific intended location has not been confirmed and remains under ⁠investigation,” the police said, adding the FBI was assisting in the probe.

Police said Paporakis is facing felony charges of “making a terrorist threat” and possessing an unlawful weapon.

The suspect appeared for a detention hearing on Wednesday and his next court appearance is scheduled for the end of October.

Human rights advocates said hate against South Asians has surged in the United States in recent years due to rising anti-immigration policies and a rise in white supremacist ideology.

articles.title: Big Walk Developer Explains Why the Game Isn't on Xbox
articles.summary: Big Walk developer House House has explained why it’s boycotting Xbox and thus why the game isn’t available on Microsoft's console.
articles.body:
Big Walk developer House House has explained why it’s boycotting Xbox and thus why the game isn’t available on Microsoft's console.

House House, the Australian studio behind Untitled Goose Game, released clever co-op puzzle adventure Big Walk earlier this year on PC, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2, leaving Xbox Series X and S out in the cold. Big Walk was critically acclaimed upon release, earning a 91 rating on Metacritic and multiple appearances on Game of the Year contender lists.

IGN’s Big Walk review returned a 9/10. We said: “Big Walk is a rewarding co-op adventure full of beautiful emergent moments as you find solutions to cleverly built puzzles and explore its vast open world with your friends.”

Since then, fans had wondered why the game failed to come out Xbox. In a statement published to its website , House House said it made the decision as part of its support for campaign group Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS), which describes itself as a “Palestinian-led movement for freedom, justice and equality.”

BDS lists Xbox as a “priority” target, and has launched a campaign calling on gamers, streamers, and developers to boycott Microsoft’s gaming efforts. As reported by the BBC , Microsoft's work with the Israeli government has been a controversial issue, including within the company itself, prompting protests by some employees.

House House indicated that it won't release Big Walk on Xbox "until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets."
