articles.title: Blue Team Only Wins 15% of Its Wardogs Games — We Asked a Color Expert Why
articles.summary: We asked a color psychologist why Blue Team only wins 15% of its Wardogs matches.
articles.body:
Wardogs is a free-for-all sandbox military game where three separate teams battle for control over an ever-changing zone in the middle of a massive map, as tanks fire shells, artillery and mortars pepper the landscape, helicopters blast the drums of war (Eiffel 65's hit song Blue (Da Ba Dee)) through proximity chat, and dozens of try-hards run and gun.

There’s Valkyra, Red Team; Manticore, Green Team; and Lonestar, Blue Team. They look different on the field, with Red rocking a soviet style, Green wearing Persian gear, and Blue looking like a Western paramilitary, but they all have access to the same equipment and have equal chance to win. So, why the hell does the Blue Team always lose?

Lonestar has become a meme in the Wardogs community. There are dozens and dozens of montages, showing them bumble and fail, missing all their shots except the ones aimed at their teammates. It’s like a David Attenborough documentary or something, watching them gear up in their spawn area as their pilots spin up and crash helicopters before even getting into the fight.

I sent a request to the Wardogs team earlier this week to find out, first off, if it’s actually true that Blue Team sucks or if we’re in some kind of meme-induced mass hallucination. According to Bulkhead, the Blue Team sucks . It’s true. The stats don’t lie. Lonestar only won around 10% of its games at the height of the “Blue Team bad” movement, but a concerted effort has been made by intrepid redditors lately to wash off the cobalt stain, resulting in Blue Team climbing to around a 15% winrate. Big woop? Red currently wins around 36% of matches, while Green takes home 49%.

“It’s something that started back in alpha. Blue was the most popular faction pre-alpha with a lot of people liking the limited lore, the American PMC aesthetic, so a lot of newer players tended to join it in alpha,” UI director Howard Philpott told IGN. “There was a genuine map advantage in the early alpha builds too which made the more competitive players swap to Red/Green and that perception persisted and spread into release.”

Some have theorized that spawn location still plays into these figures. Blue Team is located slap-bang in the middle of the map, while Green and Red are off to the sides. This leads to a perception that the Blue Team is fighting a war on two fronts, while Red and Green only have to worry about watching one side of their assault. For Season 2 , the Wardogs development team is moving team spawns on the Bakuriani map to combat this, while simultaneously launching a “social experiment to help change the perception of Lonestar.”

I reached out to color behavioral design and color psychology expert Karen Haller to get to the bottom of this. Unfortunately, Haller was just as confused as everyone else. “People would normally pick Blue first because it's first,” Haller said after I showed her the team selection screen. “So you pick the first thing, don't you? You don't go across and ignore it because that's what they're doing here. They're ignoring it and going across.”

They really are. They are massively ignoring it and going across. Every time I want to play with my friends, someone will jump in Red or Green and I’m stuck here spamming on that team to play with my mates. The entire time, Blue Team is right there, lit up and available, full of teammates who will accidentally kill you with their incompetence. It’s tempting, but my friends are in Red or Green. They fear Blue. The meme has become a mind virus infecting us all.

“It would be interesting to do a study or a comparison,” Haller said. “If [Lonestar] changed to even a dark blue, or it changed to an orange, or it changed to another color, would the perception of that team change? Because it seems to be a bit of a self-fulfilling prophecy, if I've understood it — it's not because it's Blue that they're losing.”

It’s not because it’s Blue that they’re losing. It’s because of the people who are on Blue. The ones who aren’t infected by the meme virus are — unfortunately, disproportionately — infected by incompetence instead. It’s a sad state of affairs, but it means the decent players will purposely avoid Lonestar because it’s full of the kinds of people who crash a helicopter before it’s even got off the ground or kill you by trying to revive you with a defibrillator. It was too late, Kevin. I was already revived, you bum.

It isn’t about any team being bad. It’s about groupthink, a military shooter hivemind addicted to Reddit upvotes. According to Haller, who wrote The Little Book of Color , this isn’t anything to do with color at all. If we map the teams to color theory, Red is fast like a freight train, running in and getting stuff and things done. Green would be the peacemakers, which definitely isn’t the case. But I think there’s something to Blue. “Blue is the color that you play with your mind,” Haller said. “It's intellectual, it's smart.” They’re just playing 3D chess while you’re over here running after the zone like a stupid dog with a stupid little bone. You laugh now, but let’s see how many gold bars you get for playing the objective and compare that to what Blue players end up with after spamming down hesco blocks for an entire season.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Big Walk skipped Xbox to boycott Microsoft’s involvement with Israel
articles.summary: Developer House House said it decided not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles in line with the Palestinian-led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement.
articles.body: Big Walk’s co-op multiplayer walking adventure has proved popular since launching in August, but Xbox players have been excluded from the fun — and now the game’s creators have explained why. Developer House House said in a blog post that it decided not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement, which has called to boycott Microsoft, including products under the company’s gaming division. Microsoft was named a priority BDS target in June last year over contracts it has with the Israeli military and government, with the boycott specifically calling out Xbox consoles and Game Pass subscriptions, gaming franchises owned by Microsoft, and any gaming accessories produced by the company. Microsoft’s involvement with Israel has also been protested by its own employees, and the company has fired staffers for participating in pro-Palestine demonstrations. Here’s what House House said regarding its participation in the boycott: > It has always been our intention for Big Walk to be played by groups of friends, and we know that keeping the game off Xbox runs counter to those intentions. This decision means that some people will miss out on playing Big Walk with their friends, and we understand the disappointment we’re causing. We are disappointed too. > We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets. > We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world, that coordinated collective action can confront even the most powerful interests, and that one day, Palestine will be free. > Thank you for your understanding. Big Walk is playable on Microsoft’s Windows operating system, however, as it’s available to download via Steam. We’ve asked House House why it hasn’t excluded Big Walk from Windows and will update if we hear back.

articles.title: Devious Arc Raiders Griefers Are Having Fun in PvE, Camping Locked Loot Rooms and Pulling Enemy Robots Into Extraction Points
articles.summary: Arc Raiders PvE lobbies are already stacked with griefers, using the relative safety of the mode, where your bullets don’t affect other raiders, to put other players in dangerous spots via other means, whether that be manipulating the AI, using tools, or simply getting in the way.
articles.body:
I’ve played 500 hours of Arc Raiders and I’ve seen lobbies where everyone is a serial killer and lobbies where everyone’s Santa Clause. It’s the not knowing that makes each encounter intense, but Embark’s new PvE mode removes that uncertainty. Or does it?

Arc Raiders PvE lobbies are already stacked with griefers, using the relative safety of the mode, where your bullets don’t affect other raiders, to put other players in dangerous spots via other means, whether that be manipulating the AI, using tools, or simply getting in the way.

There are already videos circulating online of players using the Bull Rush ability to bash into people who are trying to extract. This way, they die to arc enemies and can be looted without consequence, bringing a whole new level of rat behaviour to one of the rattiest games ever released.

Thread on pve mode in @ARCRaidersGame This is what pvp guys warned you about. — WhaleCalls (@whalecalls) October 13, 2026

Thread on pve mode in @ARCRaidersGame This is what pvp guys warned you about.

Outside of that, people camp the locked loot rooms and wait for another player to turn up with a key. The player with the key either opens it and shares the spoils, or they have to leave and head into another match and hope for better randoms. In PvP, you'd try to kill anyone contesting the loot. In PvE, it's a race to see who can grab it first.

There are also players using lure grenades to pull enemy robots into extraction points — this is particularly devastating when it’s a goddamn shredder. And there’s no way to be punished for playing like this.

“Legit first game on and people were being just like this, vultures, and taking all loot from Arc before you could even get anything from it,” said one X / Twitter user . “Top that off they were throwing lure grenades at me and my wife the whole time while trying to fight Arc. She went down due to it, I go for the rez then get body blocked and pushed around like I’m in grade school again.”

This could be selfish players trying to get rich at the expense of others, or it could be PvP players who want to see the mode, which is only experimental at this stage, shelved. That way, they’ll get some easy pickings back in their lobbies, after all.

Of course, the mode is currently only experimental, so Embark could make changes. I personally don’t think PvE has any place as a mode here, though — unless it were a side thing with separate unlocks. The developers say loot is nerfed, but players are coming out with some crazy gear . PvE mode landed just after Arc Raiders’ biggest update , which added grappling hooks, a new map, and more. The update sparked a resurgence of players, which Steam concurrents not seen since March.

This isn't Arc Raiders' first griefing incident, either. In December last year, soon after the game's explosive launch, one player hell bent on killing relative newcomers, casuals, and those who had next to no loot or even none at all, went viral for killing others for sport — sparking a debate about what is and isn’t acceptable PvP behavior in the process.

Bungie also announced plans to add PvE modes to Marathon as developers come to terms with extraction shooters being a niche genre. Hunt: Showdown figured this out ages ago, stuck to its cowboy-era guns, and kept its identity intact without alienating the core fans.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: WoW Forever es la excusa perfecta para volver a empezar desde cero en el MMORPG más jugado de la historia
articles.standfirst: Ya he probado el nuevo World of Wacraft Forever y no solo he regresado, sino que es muy probable que me quede una larga temporada.
articles.summary: Ya he probado el nuevo World of Wacraft Forever y no solo he regresado, sino que es muy probable que me quede una larga temporada.
articles.body: EWorld of Warcraft Forever está siendo un éxito. Disponible desde el pasado 4 de noviembre, el número de jugadores que ha regresado a Azeroth se cuenta por cientos de miles. Las primeras cifras hablan de más de un millón de personajes creados junto a un buen número de reseñas positivas, pero ¿qué es exactamente WoW Forever? ¿Por qué hay tanta gente hablando de él y qué ofrece a quienes quieren regresar al juego o descubrirlo por primera vez? La respuesta es sencilla: toma como base el Azeroth de 2004, cuyo nivel máximo era el 60, pero en una línea temporal diferente a la del World of Warcraft de toda la vida y Classic. Además de limitar el nivel a 60 y tomar como base ese Azeroth en concreto, incorpora más de 1.000 misiones nuevas. En otras palabras: aunque lleva en activo poco menos de dos semanas, sus nuevos jugadores todavía están descubriendo qué es lo que ofrece y qué novedades trae. Es una experiencia nueva que combina la esencia del original con distintas novedades. También hay nuevas zonas, como Isla de Zephras, Clarofluvial y Monte Hyjal, además de áreas originales ampliadas, nuevas mazmorras y bandas con encuentros que no formaban parte del WoW original. No repite el contenido vanilla, sino que lo utiliza como base para construir una nueva experiencia en la que incluso hay nuevas razas (los célicos), combinaciones de clase y raza inéditas hasta la fecha, modificaciones en las habilidades raciales... WoW Forever no busca ser un refrito de lo que ya hemos visto hasta ahora, sino una nueva manera de entender el MMO con el que muchos de nosotros crecimos. Es más, lo he estado probando y la verdad es que explorar sus nuevos talentos, revisar sus nuevas opciones de especialización, comprobar los cambios en las estadísticas y los nuevos objetos... Todo eso ha sido una experiencia. Podría seguir así un buen rato, y es que, aparte de todo esto, tenemos nuevos sistemas de juego, como las acampadas (que nos permiten establecer campamentos por el mundo que aportan beneficios) o los legados, desafíos que podemos completar con distintos personajes de una misma cuenta. En mi caso, llevo jugando a WoW de manera intermitente (y casual, nunca he sido un jugador que buscase optimizar tiempos ni explorar mazmorras de máxima dificultad) muchos años. No obstante, por azares del destino, llevaba un tiempo desconectado, por lo que entendí que Forever podría ser una oportunidad perfecta para regresar. En mi caso, no me he equivocado. Como usuario veterano, volver a ese mundo original con un nivel máximo tan reducido y una progresión más pausada ha sido como volver a los viejos tiempos, pero con un apartado gráfico y técnico mucho más actual. Reconectar con su mundo ha sido muy fácil, porque no ha sido necesario que me ponga al día con todas las expansiones, pero tampoco he sentido que estuviese repitiendo lo mismo que ya hice hace 15 años o lo mismo que hice allá en su momento con Classic. Es una novedad nostálgica, aunque parezca redundante. Por eso también creo que es la mejor opción para el nuevo jugador. Classic quizá se siente demasiado antiguo para muchos. El WoW normal es complicado de entender si no has estado más o menos al día. Es ahí donde entra Forever. Todos esos jugadores que estaban un poco en terreno de nadie podrían encontrar su hogar en esta nueva variante de juego. Además, en España ya se está formando una comunidad bastante amplia, y eso siempre da gusto. Al final no existe una respuesta clara, puesto que tiene un carácter netamente subjetivo. A título personal, os diría que sí. WoW Forever está resultando ser una experiencia bastante positiva desde mi perspectiva como veterano casual. Al final, buena parte del atractivo del juego clásico está en aprender a desenvolverse en Azeroth, descubrir cómo funcionan las clases y superar los obstáculos que aparecen durante la aventura. Cuando ya conoces buena parte de sus sistemas, algunas situaciones pierden ese componente de descubrimiento que las hacía especiales. Y aunque Forever incorpora novedades, no todas ellas tienen por qué resultar igual de interesantes para quienes buscan un desafío constante. Esto no significa que la experiencia sea necesariamente sencilla ni que no haya contenido exigente. Más bien, creo que su principal atractivo está en recuperar el placer de explorar, progresar y disfrutar del mundo, en lugar de centrarse exclusivamente en superar los retos más difíciles. Me parece que se adapta bien a toda clase de jugadores, desde el novato que no ha tocado World of Warcraft en su vida y siente curiosidad hasta el veterano que desconectó de la saga, pasando por el jugador de toda la vida que busca algo diferente y los que quieren darle otra vuelta al juego. Quizá donde menos destaque sea en el apartado hardcore, ya que la limitación de nivel —por muchas zonas nuevas que haya— y la experiencia acumulada hacen que ciertos retos no se sientan tan desafiantes.

articles.title: Rock Hard Platformer 'Refund This Game' Challenges You to Beat It Within Steam’s 2-Hour Refund Window
articles.summary: If you’ve played Baby Steps or Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy, you’ll understand the pure allure of a game that makes you want to clench your jaw so hard your teeth shoot off and ricochet around the room. One developer has taken this genre to its logical conclusion, challenging players to beat it in two hours so they can request their $3.99 back from Steam.
articles.body:
If you’ve played Baby Steps or Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy, you’ll understand the pure allure of a game that makes you want to clench your jaw so hard your teeth shoot off and ricochet around the room. One developer has taken this genre to its logical conclusion, challenging players to beat it in two hours so they can request their $3.99 back from Steam.

'Refund This Game' is a challenging 3D platformer where you’re tasked with reaching the summit in under two hours. Your reward for doing it? You can legitimately request a refund (and be granted one, no questions asked) under Valve’s own refund policy rules on Steam.

“Fling yourself up to the top in this Getting Over It-like 3D platformer!” the developers wrote on the official Steam page . “Stick your pole to walls, bend it and fling yourself with great speed! One mistake means falling all the way down. Can you reach the summit in under two hours and EARN that refund?!”

In the game, you pole vault your way through a psychedelic cyberspace of shapes and colors. You only get a single checkpoint, which you can place anywhere you want on the course.

It’s a smart bit of marketing for this specific kind of YouTube baity game — especially as it includes leaderboards for those who decide not to claim their money back. The Steam page also teases a secret endgame challenge, but you’ll probably have to dedicate more than two hours to figure that out.

In July this year, developers criticized Steam’s two-hour refund policy . The debate started with a post from the developer behind indie boat adventure Paddle Paddle Paddle, which had positive Steam reviews from people who proudly enjoyed the game, got their time out of it, then refunded it.

"Would be cool if you could finally do something about your refund policy," the developer said. "Got dozens of reviews like that and 21% refund rate even though the reviews are 90% Very Positive. That's over 55,000 Refunds btw…"

Valve already includes a section on "abuse" of its refund policy in the platform's terms and conditions, which states that refunds were not "a way to get free games" — and anyone unfairly taking advantage of this would have their refund privileges suspended. As someone who’s been covering the industry for the past 15 years, I’ve never seen evidence of this policy being enforced, however.

Steam’s refund policy is obviously a good thing for consumers, but there’s probably room to make it more nuanced for shorter indie games. These are generally made by very small teams, while mammoth triple-A games walk away from the policy relatively unscathed.

As for Refund This Game, it's currently sat on a 'Positive' user review rating on Steam, although there aren't many reviews yet (it only launched on October 12). One Steam review, from a person who had 1.9 hours of playtime at the time they reviewed it, and currently 5.5 hours on record, called on players not to refund the game if they enjoyed it.

"The game is fun, it's a nice challenge though I think you shouldn't refund games that you have enjoyed if its a reasonable price which it is," they said.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: GTA 6's Level of Detail Is So Extreme, Rockstar Built an Entire Scripted System Just for Sweat
articles.summary: Rockstar Games is of course known for its attention to detail, with previous Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption games raising the bar for realism. GTA 6, though, looks set to go further than any video game before it, with a dedicated system that determines how much the characters sweat.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games is of course known for its attention to detail, with previous Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption games raising the bar for realism. GTA 6 , though, looks set to go further than any video game before it, with a dedicated system that determines how much the characters sweat.

Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier said in a new video accompaniment to his making of GTA 6 article published this week, that Rockstar told him of a scripted system in the game that makes dual protagonists Jason and Lucia — or, it sounds like, any character in the game — exert different amounts of sweat depending on how much effort they’re putting into whatever activity they’re doing.

So, in a nightclub, for example, Lucia will sweat more if she’s putting a lot of effort into dancing. Similarly, the harder Jason works out, the more he’ll sweat. We might have already seen GTA 6's sweat system in action. In the Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look video released in August, we briefly see Lucia dancing in a nightclub, and there's a distinct glisten to her skin that suggests she's sweating. Or maybe it's a trick of the light.

This shows the incredible level of detail in GTA 6 — above and beyond any video game ever made — but it also helps explain why GTA 6 took so long to develop (eight years in terms of proper development work), and why it cost so much money to make ( not more than $1.5 billion, but no doubt the most expensive video game of all time ).

Indeed, as the Bloomberg article reveals, Rockstar set up a new studio in Los Angeles packed with writers, producers, and directors, just to make NPCs.

GTA 6 has suffered a number of high-profile delays, each of which has been explained publicly as part of Rockstar’s mission to achieve video game perfection with this game. When you hear about the sweat that’s poured into it, you start to understand what this will actually look like when the game itself comes out.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

With GTA 6 out next month, we’ve got plenty more for you to sink your teeth into, including our in-depth interview with Rockstar North's Rob Nelson in full, our report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , and some of the unusual marketing rockstar has put in place.

articles.title: GTA 6 Will Make The Game Awards Cutoff Date for Eligibility by the Skin of Its Teeth, Confirming It Has a Chance at 2026 Game of the Year
articles.summary: GTA 6 is officially in with a chance of winning the 2026 Game of the Year award at this year’s The Game Awards, after the show confirmed the cutoff date for eligibility.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is officially in with a chance of winning the 2026 Game of the Year award at this year’s The Game Awards, after the show confirmed the cutoff date for eligibility.

According to a FAQ on The Game Awards website , to be in with a chance of winning an award a game must be released on or before Friday, November 20, 2026. GTA 6’s release date is currently November 19, 2026, which means it’s made the cutoff date by just a single day.

What is the Cutoff Date for Eligibility?

Games must be made commercially available to customers on or before Friday, November 20, 2026, at 9 p.m. PT. In the Players’ Voice category, games must ship on or before November 30, 2026.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Nominations for this year’s awards haven’t been announced yet, of course, but it’s hard to imagine a situation where GTA 6 doesn’t show up for most, if not all, the categories it’s eligible for. Sandfall Interactive's Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 holds the world record for the most wins at The Game Awards , taking home a whopping nine awards at last year's show. Will GTA 6 beat it?

And given GTA Online 2 or whatever the multiplayer mode ends up being called is reportedly due out next year, perhaps alongside a PC version , we could see GTA 6 back in contention at The Game Awards 2027.

While we wait for this year's nominations, we’ve got plenty more on GTA 6 for you to check out, including our in-depth interview with Rockstar North's Rob Nelson , our report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , and confirmation of GTA 6’s sweat system .

articles.title: Clash Royale: The Grand Arena Board Game Exclusive Trailer and Kickstarter Reveal
articles.body:
Maestro Media recently announced a new board game adaptation of the popular mobile game Clash Royale . Now, IGN can exclusively reveal that Maestro Media will be launching a Kickstarter campaign in support of the final product: Clash Royale: The Grand Arena this month

The Kickstarter, which is aiming to launch on October 20, follows the successful crowdfunding of Maestro’s previous collaboration with Supercell, Clash of Clans: The Epic Raid . Ahead of the campaign, we got the chance to speak with the board game’s lead designer, David Gordon, about how the team approached bringing the mobile hit to the tabletop.

First, we learned a little more about what to expect from the board game itself, which you can get the gist of in this exclusive trailer:

The Grand Arena generally adapts the deck-building and strategy elements of the mobile app into a board game. Yep, that means fans will finally be able to build Clash Royale decks with real cardboard.

The tabletop game is designed for two to four players. Each player controls their own forces, which consist of eight-card decks built around a chosen Champion. Cards will be based on the mobile game’s card list, plenty of which feature characters and items going back to the original Clash of Clans era.

In-game, players take turns to try and destroy other players’ Towers while also protecting their own. The board features two lanes, and players must determine where exactly to play cards to launch attacks, plant defensive units, and use items. Players can’t endlessly cycle through their cards, either, as moves are limited by the classic Clash resource, Elixir.

Destroying another player’s Tower nets you a Crown, and the player with the most Crowns at the end wins.

Sound familiar? It should - at least to Clash Royale fans. Maestro Media put some serious thought into translating the mobile gameplay to the tabletop.

We asked the game’s lead designer, David Gordon, about how the team approached the game’s design, and learned the process took some trial and error: “We tried mechanisms such as actual real time play against a clock, putting out a bunch of cubes, and simultaneous reveals, as well as various strategies to minimize the admin for players. Ultimately, we found that focusing on elixir spending in a turn-based card play system yielded a fun experience that most resembled that of the video game.”

That said, the team behind The Grand Arena was weary of designing a game that would only appeal to die-hard Clash fans. Over the course of the game’s development, they play-tested The Grand Arena with both Clash veterans and people who had no experience with the Supercell franchise. In Gordon’s words, “It was important that a strategy game fan who had never played the video game would find the tabletop version fun - and hopefully even inspire them to try the video game!”

The Grand Arena will be joining Maestro Media's previous release, Clash of Clans: The Epic Raid, which was successfully supported on Kickstarter in 2025 and is now available from retailers like Amazon and Target .

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Crystal Lake Finally Introduces a Key Missing Component of Jason Voorhees’ History
articles.summary: The new prequel series Crystal Lake both rewrites and adds to Friday the 13th history -- including a key missing component of Jason Voorhees' backstory.
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for Crystal Lake Season 1, which is available on Peacock now.

After 17 years since the last entry in the franchise, filled with movies that failed to get off the ground followed by a protracted legal battle over the rights that prevented any new projects from moving forward, the Friday the 13th series has finally risen from a watery grave with Crystal Lake , the new eight-episode Peacock series.

Set in the early 1970s, the series goes back to the roots of the franchise by focusing on Pamela Voorhees (Linda Cardellini, taking on the role made famous by Betsy Palmer), the killer in the original Friday the 13th . Here, we follow the supposed drowning death of her son, Jason (Callum Vinson), and how she reacts to it in the aftermath, charting her descent into madness and murder that we saw in that 1980 movie – before she got her head cut off and her son took over the series in the second film.

By the end of the season, some major revelations have been made that reveal important aspects of the Voorhees family history that have never been delved into before across the 12 Friday the 13th movies, some which are no doubt already proving to be quite polarizing among fans. That includes a key aspect of Jason Voorhees’ history that answers a lot of questions! Let’s dive into what we learned, how it fits into the movie series, and where it diverges from it.

And, of course, who lived and who died...

Crystal Lake has a big surprise actor and character pop up in its sixth episode, when we meet Elias Wittering, played by Midnight Mass/Gen V/Widow’s Bay veteran Hamish Linklater. If you’re a big Friday the 13th fan, just seeing the name Elias (not spoken in that episode, but revealed in the closing credits), you knew exactly who he had to be: Jason’s father!

We’ve never met Jason’s dad in any Friday the 13th movie, but we nearly did in 1986’s Friday the 13th Part VI: Jason Lives , which was going to introduce Elias Voorhees. And though the scene written for the character was cut and never filmed, his name managed to stick around as part of the lore, said aloud for the first time in 1993’s Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday , while we’d also see versions of the character included or referenced in other Friday the 13th stories, including in comic books and Friday the 13th: The Game .

Linklater is a pretty great get for the series as far as bringing in another acclaimed actor to play Jason’s dad alongside recent Emmy-winner Cardellini as his mom. But of course, it’s also notable that Elias, as envisioned here, isn't a Voorhees here at all, since we learn early on that Pamela only took on that name after going on the run with Jason.

The show’s seventh episode reveals Pamela and Elias’ full history, and how Pamela Scott was a nightclub singer with a burgeoning career in 1959 New York before she nearly suffered a miscarriage with the child she was carrying with her boyfriend, Elias. Elias Wittering was a salesman for the huge company Bellflower Chemical, and he took her to a state of the art medical facility the company had in Houston, Texas, where they not only said the baby could be saved, but would be given special treatments to help him.

In the midst of this, Pamela and Elias were married, making her Mrs. Wittering, and everything seemed hunky-dory at first. Until…

In what will no doubt be the most debated and controversial plot point in Crystal Lake amongst the Friday the 13th fanbase, it turns out that the treatments Bellflower were giving both to Pamela and to other pregnant women were in fact designed to enhance human durability, with the ultimate goal of making people better able to survive what Bellflower saw as an inevitable nuclear war (it was the Cold War, don’t forget!). Elias was fully aware of all of this, keeping it a secret from Pamela, while allowing the scientists to perform dangerous procedures on his wife and child.

These “Project Argonaut” experiments resulted in deformed babies, many of whom died, and none of whom were able to live anything resembling a normal life, except for one… And his name was Jason. Yep, that’s right: Crystal Lake gives the first-ever genuine overarching explanation for both why Jason looks the way he does, but more importantly, why he just won’t stay dead despite all that happens to him throughout the franchise. Why didn’t Jason actually die from his drowning? Why did he survive multiple would-be fatal wounds in Friday the 13th Parts 2, 3 and 4? Why was he able to be resurrected by a lightning bolt as a freaking zombie from Part 6 on? It was because of Bellflower!

As Elias puts it, “Trauma actually makes him stronger. In fact, it could spur accelerated physical growth!” Amusingly, this not only helps account for Jason’s form when we see him return from the lake in this very show (more on that below), but even his increasingly hulking form in the movies, where ever larger actors kept being cast to play him. Oh, and Pamela being so mentally disturbed? Also Bellflower’s fault, as they gave her experimental mood stabilizers that altered her brain chemistry, and which she no longer was using after learning the truth and escaping to her new life and her fake identity in Crystal Lake with Jason.

There were fans already bristling about the hints at this storyline in the show’s trailers, preferring Pamela and Jason remain nothing more than a small town New Jersey mother and son prior to his drowning and the events of the first film. And I get that, but also… Friday the 13th is a ridiculous series! And I say that as someone who adores these movies and has watched each of them dozens of times. But certainly from the moment they even decided Jason didn’t drown as a kid after all, in order to bring him back as an adult killer in Part 2, the series has had little connection to anything grounded. And that was before the sequels included Jason’s aforementioned transformation into an outright zombie, revealing his soul could jump from body to body via a demonic snake-like creature, and his trip to outer space.

Speaking of that last example, while everyone remembers 2002’s Jason X as the one where Jason is on a spaceship hundreds of years in the future, it’s worth recalling the film’s prologue, which is set in 2008 and shows how Jason ends up cryogenically frozen. That was one of the only times an entry in the series so directly acknowledged the bizarreness of Jason’s biology, arguably directly setting up what Crystal Lake has now explained.

In that film, Jason has been captured and taken to the “Crystal Lake Research Facility,” a place we can presume was eventually built expressly because of the town’s most famous resident. After multiple failed execution attempts, the US government now actively wants to experiment on Jason instead, with Dr. Wimmer (played by freaking David Cronenberg!) arguing that “His unique ability to regenerate lost and damaged tissue, it cries out for more research.” If only Dr. Wimmer had known about Bellflower and what they were up to, he’d have his answers.

The fifth episode of Crystal Lake features a near shot for shot recreation of the opening sequence of Friday the 13th, as horny Camp Crystal Lake counselors Barry and Claudette (played here by Phoenix Parnevik and Danielle Kotch) sneak off together to do what horny counselors do. As in the film, we get a POV shot of the killer attacking Barry and Claudette, but this time we continue past what the film shows, as we reveal Pamela Voorhees walking in on a murder already in process, rather than committing it herself. And the actual killer here isn’t Jason, the most likely second possibility, it’s… Grace!

Who is Grace? Played by Gwendolyn Sundstrom, she’s in many ways Crystal Lake’s most intriguing new character, a 13-year old girl who was Jason’s only real friend before he drowned, treating him with kindness while everyone else ignored or bullied him. There are a lot of extenuating circumstances to Grace becoming a killer, as the poor kid was in a bad place after her mom recently died (killed by Pamela, unbeknownst to her). She was also spending time with an older group of hippie kids whose irresponsible ways led Grace to take three tabs of acid before she went full Voorhees on Barry and Claudette while tripping out of her mind, having blamed them for what happened to Jason because she had spotted them hooking up while he was drowning in the lake.

The next day, Grace is confused by what actually happened, even as Pamela feeds her the story she wants her to tell the authorities about one of the hippies, Harmony (Manon Gage), being responsible for not just Barry and Claudette’s murders, but for the rest of the hippie group, who Pamela herself slaughtered. We don’t see Grace again after Episode 6, but she’s obviously a notable character to continue to follow in potential future seasons. Does she actually remember what she did or could it come back to her, along with Pamela coldly finishing off Claudette, who was still bleeding out after Grace stabbed her? Is this a tragic event she’ll move on from, or are we seeing yet another full-fledged Friday the 13th killer rise up alongside Pamela, Jason and Part 5’s Roy ? Hell, could her past friendship lead to some twisted Jason’s Murder Girlfriend deal down the line!?

Crystal Lake reveals that Pamela killed way more people than just Barry and Claudette prior to the massacre that Friday the 13th centers on, with her building up quite a body count throughout the season. But as it turns out, Jason was also already busy with his own murders prior to seeing his mom decapitated.

We get glimpses of some of this early in the season, including a girl Jason kills and skins (!), leaving her body at the home of Crazy Ralph (Nick Cordileone). But the finale gives us the full reveal of the post-drowning Jason, with Elias being correct about that trauma-induced growth spurt, because a year later, he’s notably larger (and played by Jonathan Tison) than before. We get some fun elements pulled in from Friday the 13th Part 2 here as well, including the shack Jason used as a home (and a shrine to his mother) in that film, revealed as an abandoned place Jason and Grace used to go to before the drowning.

Plus, we see Jason in a version of his Part 2 look, wearing the one-eyed burlap sack he used as his first mask, prior to Part 3 giving him the iconic hockey mask. Amusingly, they even do a prequel overexplanation move by having Pamela, in the wake of finding the cabin thanks to Grace, leaving him food and supplies in a sack that he clearly decides to use to cover his face afterwards.

At the end of the finale, Elias, having tracked Pamela to Crystal Lake, chases her to that shack, where mother, father, and son are reunited… And Jason treats his crappy father as you’d expect, crushing his head between his hands. Jason then actually begins to choke Pamela, nearly killing his mother too, until memories of her love for him stops him. He’s then shot in the head by Ralph, which could perhaps further explain his simplistic, animalistic state in the films, though he already seemed pretty well there, given he was already in the whole mute murderer mode, presumably as a result of lack of oxygen from the drowning, combined with more Project Argonaut fallout, since he no longer was taking his own medication that helped him when he had seizures as a boy.

Regardless, Jason shakes off the gunshot (not the last time that will happen) and flees, as an unhinged Pamela rants about how these woods belong to her and her son, and everyone needs to stay away from the lake and the camp. This shows her mindset going into Friday the 13th, while also revealing that she actually does have full knowledge that Jason is out there, even as she’s also actively killing counselors in an ill-placed sense of revenge and speaking to herself as the younger Jason. Pamela’s got a lot going on!

Showrunner Brad Caleb Kane has referred to Crystal Lake as a “spiritual prequel” to Friday the 13th, because it’s clearly not meant to line up exactly with the established canon of that movie. This is explicit from the get-go, when Jason drowns in 1971, not 1957, as he did in that film, while the brunt of the season – and Barry and Claudette’s deaths the summer after the drowning – occurs in 1972, not 1958.

But still, it feels like the idea here is that minus those years being different – and the major events being added throughout including a lot more earlier murders around Crystal Lake than we knew of previously, albeit with out of towners mostly taking the blame for them – the events of the show are intended to eventually lead into the circa-1980 events of the film. Presumably, that means that all of the characters in the show who are also in the movie (including Deputy Dorf, Crazy Ralph, Trudy the diner owner, and Enos the truck driver) are safe if we get future seasons, because they need to be around for the movie’s events.

But that also means you have the Ahsoka prequel factor: the characters who are not i n the movie and have to be gotten rid of at some point, whether that be by their death or them leaving for whatever reason. This includes the aforementioned Grace, but also other key players like Sheriff Levon Brooks (William Catlett) and his sister, Briana (Devin Kessler). Levon in particular stands out, since we meet plenty of other Crystal Lake cops in the Friday the 13th films, but never this particular sheriff, who notably has a romantic relationship with Pamela in the first season.

Does this mean Levon is doomed (DOOMED!)? Or could he simply depart Crystal Lake at some point? Or could they say he was still sheriff by Friday the 13th, but simply remained offscreen, ready to get some very bad news about a woman he cared about?

And then there’s Harmony, the Hippie Who Got Away. Pamela and Grace claim she was the killer, but Harmony saw for herself it was Pamela who murdered her friends, even if she also was tripping at the time it happened. That seems like a problem that could easily circle back around for Pamela at some point, which she’d have to figure out how to solve.

Perhaps we’ll find out the answer to these questions and more if Crystal Lake returns for Season 2.

articles.title: Sega Pulls Disastrous Total War: Shogun 2 Remaster From Sale Following Backlash
articles.summary: Creative Assembly and Sega have pulled Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition from Steam after a raft of complaints about the quality of the remaster.
articles.body:
Creative Assembly and Sega have pulled Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition from Steam after a raft of complaints about the quality of the remaster.

Released on October 13, this facelift for the much-loved 2011 strategy classic should have been a slam dunk for Creative Assembly. Sega had trumpeted "upgraded visuals," which include "improved textures, models, lighting, shadows, fog and environments, alongside modern rendering, anti-aliasing and upscaling options." The game also has optional 2.5D campaign movies inspired by Japanese Ukiyo-e art.

But fans quickly noticed art inconsistencies that some alleged were evidence of low quality AI use. In one image, a samurai’s face was replaced with a metallic texture that struggled to distinguish between the face and helmet. Fans also pointed out inconsistencies on the new storyboard cutscenes.

The "Complete Edition" release of Shogun 2 Total War was so badly received that it might be pulled from sale on Steam. Over the years I've had many Japan-loving international students who played the original game, but the "upgrade" has bugs and what looks like bad AI upscaling. — Jeffrey J. Hall 🇯🇵🇺🇸 (@mrjeffu) October 15, 2026

The "Complete Edition" release of Shogun 2 Total War was so badly received that it might be pulled from sale on Steam. Over the years I've had many Japan-loving international students who played the original game, but the "upgrade" has bugs and what looks like bad AI upscaling.

Compounding the issue was the fact that Sega pulled the original Shogun 2 from sale, forcing customers to buy the new Complete Edition instead if they wanted to play. The original game was often on sale for a few dollars, while this remaster was priced $40.

Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition currently sits on an “overwhelmingly negative” user review rating on Steam, as customers who paid $10 to “upgrade” the game aired their grievances.

“We’re aware that Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards,” Creative Assembly and Sega said in a joint statement. “We’ve seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be.

Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition Screenshots

“As a result we are working with platform holders to remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues. Existing owners will still be able to access and play the game.

“We are working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 – Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War.”

The wording of the statement shines a light on Polish co-development studio Mataboo, which has worked on everything from The Blood of Dawnwalker to Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League. Upcoming Creative Assembly games include the hotly anticipated Total War: Warhammer 40,000 and Alien Isolation 2.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: The Pokémon x Beats Pill Special Edition Speaker Is Now Available at Select Retailers
articles.body:
Beats by Dre teased a collaboration with Pokémon earlier this week. We now know what exactly that collaboration involves: a new Pokémon-themed Beats Pill.

The special-edition Beats Pill features images of two Pokémon: Pikachu and Mimikyu. Yep, a Gen 7 Pokméon is actually getting some merch love. The wireless speaker, which joins the endless list of Pokémon’s 30th anniversary celebrations, is now available at both Apple and Target for $149.99.

Pokemon Edition Beats Pill Speaker Now Available

The special-edition émon speaker is a new colorway for the latest Beats Pill. This model was originally released in 2024 with an MSRP of $149.99, the same price as the new Pokémon edition.

The big upgrade was sound quality. The 2024 upgrade comes with a re-designed "racetrack" woofer that displaces up to 90% more air for a clearer bass and less distortion. A slightly tilted angle also helps project the speaker’s sound into listeners’ ears instead of toward the table or floor. While the new model returned to mono architecture, you can pair it with another Beats Pill for Amplify or Stereo Mode.

The wireless speaker offers up to 24 hours of battery life in addition to a quick-charging “Fast Fuel” mode that gets you two hours of battery life off of 10 minutes of charging. It comes with USB-C connectivity and supports reverse charging, meaning you can use the speaker as a power bank for your phone or other compatible devices.

The speaker is also rated IP67 for dust and water resistance, making it a great pick for pool parties and beach days.

As for the Pokémon design? Well, it’s… interesting. The speaker itself is largely grey, with Mimikyu appearing in a grey-scale. Color is reserved for the classic yellow hues and red cheeks of Pikachu, who has a somewhat confused expression. Small lightning bolt details decorate the surrounding speaker.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: ‘I Can Really Nitpick Things’ – Firearms Expert Jonathan Ferguson Explains the Most Common Gun Mistakes in Games
articles.summary: We spoke to the internet's favorite firearms expert, Jonathan Ferguson, about all the things games get wrong about guns and his work on Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.
articles.body:
Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has a familiar voice hiding in its loadout menu. Click on any gun or grenade and you can listen to an audio description voiced by none other than Jonathan Ferguson, Keeper of Firearms and Artillery at the Royal Armouries Museum in Leeds . Ferguson has become something of a cult figure at the intersection of firearms history and video games, thanks to his detailed breakdowns of video game weapons on YouTube, but he also now plays a part in the development of video games, thanks to the Royal Armouries' consultation service. He’s worked with studios such as Team17, Facepunch, and Rebellion to ensure their weapons are as accurate as possible and avoid commonly-made mistakes, such as getting shotguns completely wrong.

"The most persistent [mistake] that you still occasionally see is shotguns being completely less than lethal, or non-lethal, even, at a set distance," Ferguson tells me, although he does note that “I think a lot of developers have wised up on this.”

It's certainly true that the years of shotguns effectively being little more than loud knives is drawing to a close, across not only mil-sims but blockbusters, too. Both Insurgency: Sandstorm and Red Dead Redemption 2 are notable for their more realistic depictions of shotguns.

"The more and more detail we see incorporated in games, the more they're able to make it resemble reality a bit more,” Ferguson tells me.

There are few people better-equipped to answer a developer’s questions about firearms than Ferguson, who not only reacts to in-game guns for the EXP YouTube channel but is also a gamer himself. His understanding of the needs of gameplay over raw historical accuracy made him an ideal fit for consulting on Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, although developer Expression Games’ realistic depiction of shotguns with authentic (even slightly generous) range is less to do with his consultancy than the studio doing its homework across the era’s entire arsenal.

“I didn't need to tell them that the K50M submachine gun existed and was specific to the North Vietnamese,” explains Ferguson. “They already knew that. So they'd done their due diligence there."

Beyond the shotgun issue, Ferguson often finds himself picking up on minutiae. "There are lots of little tiny details, like realistic patterns of cartridge case ejection for example,” he tells me, “which really don't matter to how the game is played, but if you notice them, adds to it.”

Through his appearances on Firearms Expert Reacts videos, Ferguson has built a reputation for picking apart the details many players won’t even notice. And so in the matter of case ejection patterns, he recognises there’s a bigger picture.

“There is a difference between criticising or observing, reacting, and actually playing,” he says. “There are a number of games where either I've played them previously and then I'm being asked to comment on them, or I haven't played them yet but I do later, and I realise, ‘oh that thing I commented on, I didn't notice at all’, because my attention is where it should be: on the gameplay, the story, the enemies, whatever."

Increased visual fidelity is something of a double-edged sword when it comes to these kind of problems. During the the days of Doom and Quake, no one expected ejecting shells to be animated to reflect reality. Today, when so many items in games are rendered to reflect real-world physics, we expect to see something more realistic.

"That's the kind of level of detail we're at,” says Ferguson. “I can really nitpick things, and it gets increasingly hard to actually nitpick that stuff [because the detail has become so good]. Occasionally, I find out that's because of something I've said, which is kind of rewarding, but I also feel bad because it's making people do extra work."

Sometimes, the quest for realism can require games to become less realistic to feel just right. Ferguson explains that pistol slides are a good example of this – in video games, it’s better if they move much slower than they do in reality.

"If you can see them moving, that showcases the animator's skill. Things aren't clipping through each other and it looks cool,” he explains. “In reality, if you shoot a gun, even if you stare right at that moving part, you can't really see it move. It's kind of faster than your eye can realistically perceive.

“But [a player’s] expectation is, 'well I know that bit of a gun moves', and [if] they don't see something move, or it moves really fast and they can't really tell, they might think, 'oh, that's not very satisfying'."

Ferguson himself also wasn't immune to a misplaced sense of realism during his youth, years before he became an expert at the Royal Armouries.

"I'll never forget firing up GoldenEye 64 for the first time,” he says. “Something about the way the AK was represented in that, the sound of it, the muzzle flash, the way you could sort of wave it about, that felt so much like, ‘oh, that's like a real rifle.’

“Of course, it's not at all,” he adds. “Especially when you look in third person, it looks like they're just one-handing the thing. But in ‘97, that was super impressive."

GoldenEye's version of the AK-47 may not have been realistic, but the assault rifle it is based on occupies a unique position in popular culture. It has become a symbol as much as a weapon, used and recognised across the entire planet. If anything has achieved the status of “meta” in the real world, as weapons do in games, it’s the AK-47.

"That distinctive profile, especially with the steeply curved magazine of the 7.62x39 original version, is an absolute icon,” Ferguson says. “A literal icon. I don't use ‘iconic’ in the lazy way, I use it in a literal way, because it appears on the flag of Mozambique for this very reason. It's a tool of liberation for some, a tool of terrorism and violence for others."

Of course, move across the globe to Europe and North America and there’s another assault rifle that could claim the same thing. "I think certainly the Western world would say AR-15,” he says. “A short-barreled AR-15 with a telescopic stock and a flat top. That's kind of the go-to for all sorts of people."

While “meta” has a deeper meaning, it’s often perceived as “the popular weapon everyone uses”, and what’s popular in one medium can directly influence what’s used in another. Ferguson’s deep knowledge of firearms, video games, and pop-culture means he’s able to spot how one medium’s fascination with a certain weapon creates a sort of “feedback loop”. One particularly notable example is the use of "the specific chopped, converted HK94 that was used in several ‘80s action movies, including, most famously, Die Hard" in the GTA games.

But while movies have long had a widespread influence on video games, Ferguson notes that the tide is somewhat turning: "Games have been in the shadow of movies, but I think they've moved beyond it." The first example that he reaches for doesn’t have anything to do with guns at all, but Ferguson notes that Spider-Man: Brand New Day uses "fight scenes and finishing moves taken from the Insomniac games. Obviously, that was the inspiration. I think we'll see that with guns as well."

But while we’re still at the dawn of video games impacting the armouries of movies, Ferguson notes that video games already have a profound impact on the consumer habits of gun owners.

"Obviously, they buy stuff that's in the movies, but there's that much more personal connection to what they feel they've used, because they've grown up playing games,” he explains. “So there's a feedback loop from non-interactive media to video games to the real world, and it goes round and round. And, of course, quite a few people join up to armed services as well, having watched those movies, played those games. "

With video games directly influencing the way the public interact with guns, be that purchases or becoming involved in the military, I wanted to know whether Ferguson believed that the depiction of firearms in games has helped or hindered the public understanding of these weapons. For many gamers, who live in countries with stringent gun laws, firearms are rarely seen and even more rarely handled. Video games are often our only window into the use of guns, and they can sometimes give us the wrong idea about their real-world usage. However, Ferguson believes that the opposite is true, at least to some extent, noting that games can provide a fairly strong base understanding of the roles of various guns in warfare.

"I think [games can offer weapon knowledge] in terms of how they look and their technical accuracy and maybe a little bit of an idea of what they're for. In other words, what's a rifle for versus a pistol versus a shotgun".

He notes that, in particular, we are now seeing more depictions of 18th and 19th century firearms, as well as those from World War I. "I think moving out of living memory has made that more of a thing," he adds. "[There are] more and better depictions of guns, from my point of view as someone who studies this stuff, than ever, and [video games are] one of the best ways to get a grounding of what's out there, what's it for, who used it and what for."

He is, however, quick to point out the limitations of the medium. "Media can't give you a full sense of what it's like to shoot a gun, much less to take one into combat or defend a home with it or whatever. They're two separate things."

And yet, while simulation and reality are two separate things, the two will forever be entwined… and they have been entwined for far longer than the existence of video games. Ferguson notes how his interest in firearms in modern popular culture had "raised eyebrows" from his predecessors, despite the fact that they themselves had established their interest in firearms through cowboy movies. But while some in the firearms community may grumble, Ferguson is well aware that the link between guns and video games isn’t going away anytime soon. If anything, it will only become more important to study and consult on.

"I still meet people who don't play games at all,” says Ferguson. “Sometimes, on [the Royal Armouries YouTube] channel, we get comments saying, ‘oh, God, not more video game content.’ But I'm sorry, there are lots of us out there playing and consuming media, and that's not going away."

articles.title: Diablo 5 Inches Closer to Launch as Cinematics Work Begins
articles.summary: Diablo 5 is still a few years away, but it looks like development is trucking along, now that Blizzard has started filming for its cinematics.
articles.body:
Diablo 5 is still a few years away , but it looks like development is trucking along, now that Blizzard has started filming for its cinematics.

Blizzard cinematic director Neil David Carter posted a photo of the motion capture stage on X / Twitter , simply saying "First shoot #Diablo5." If the cinematic team is just starting motion capture, Diablo 5 probably isn't super late in its development. However, if the cinematic team is shooting motion capture for cutscenes, then the story is mostly fleshed out already.

Luckily, in an interview with Windows Central, senior producer Tiffany Watt confirmed that Diablo 5 would be using its own fork of the Diablo 4 engine, so at least the team didn't have to start building the game from scratch. But in a game like Diablo 5, a lot of work has to go into balance, itemization and world design, and the new game is likely going to be a bit more complicated than Diablo 4 thanks to the procedurally generated maps.

First shoot #Diablo5 — Neil David Carter (@NeilDavidCarter) October 14, 2026

That's why some folks, like former co-founder of Path of Exile developer Grinding Gear Games , are skeptical that Diablo 5 is going to hit its targeted release date. After all, if Diablo 5 does launch in spring 2029, it will come out just shy of six years after Diablo 4. There was an 11-year gap between Diablo 3 and Diablo 4. The gap between Diablo 4 and Diablo 5, if all goes according to plan, will be about half as long. It's little wonder, then, that Blizzard has had to work hard to convince its players that it's not abandoning Diablo 4 early, and that the game will still get content even after Diablo 5 launches .

Only time will be able to tell whether or not Diablo 4 will continue to get updates, or will just get a handful of seasons on repeat like Diablo 3 after Diablo 4 launched. But, really, all we can do is wait and see how everything plays out. For what it's worth, Diablo 5 is shaping up to be a totally different ARPG than its predecessor, and I can't wait to see how the cinematics they're shooting now are going to turn out.

Diablo 5 will tell 'three stories,' including the past, the present desolation of Diablo's takeover, and the future 'terror forming' of Sanctuary. Diablo 5 is set roughly one century after Diablo 4, in a post-apocalyptic timeline where the Lord of Terror himself has already won and rules over a fallen Sanctuary.

articles.title: 33 New Details From the GTA 6 Launch Trailer
articles.summary: GTA 6's launch trailer may only be 90 seconds long, but there's plenty to see - here's the 33 details we spotted.
articles.body:
Yet another look at GTA 6 has come our way, which means it’s time to get forensic; we’ve gone through the new trailer with a fine-tooth comb to pick out all of the interesting details hidden within. From peeks at what’s in store for some of its most explosive missions, further insights into Jason’s military past, and more than one visit to a steamy shower, there’s plenty of new things to take a look at.

Let’s not waste any more time. Here are the 33 details we spotted in the GTA 6 launch trailer.

Multiple shots offer a closer look at Jason and paint a pretty clear picture of the kind of man we’ll be taking control of. We already knew that he was ex-military, but midway through the trailer we see him wearing a U.S. Army t-shirt that offers more details on his service.

1. Firstly, the combat training school Jason seemingly trained at is located in North Fort Law. Long-time fans will recognise this as the military base from the very first Grand Theft Auto game. In that original game, it was located in the state of New Guernsey, but it’s more likely that the one Jason attended is in the State of Alderney, the HD universe’s take on New Jersey. We know that Lucia is from Liberty City, which is located in the neighboring State of Liberty – perhaps they met when Jason was stationed at the base?

2. More prominent than that small print is the word “Marauder”, which matches the skull-and-parachute tattoo on Jason’s arm that we’ve seen in previous videos. The Marauders are presumably the unit he served in, and may be a reference to the real-life Merrill's Marauders, a 1940s special forces group. Its modern-day equivalent is the 75th Ranger Regiment, and so it’s likely that Jason was a ranger.

3. It seems like Jason has fallen on tough times since he left the forces. “I got in some trouble in the army, didn’t leave on the best of terms,” he says in the trailer’s opening. “They don’t give loans, anything, to people like me.” With a situation like that, it’s no wonder Jason has resorted to crime. The cost of living is only going up!

4. Thankfully, it seems like Jason’s experience in the Marauders has equipped him with all the tools for a very fruitful life of crime. We see him wading through water dressed in special forces-like infiltration gear, a pair of night-vision goggles on his head and a silenced assault rifle in his hands. He’s accompanied by two other men, and the trio seem to have disembarked from a boat. While the blush night sky certainly looks very Floridian (or should we say Leonidan), an odd reptile to the left of the scene appears to be a komodo dragon, which are native to Indonesia. Is this a flashback to a mission from Jason’s army days? Or is the reptile simply a native of Leonida’s wetlands, and Jason has perhaps called on some former squadmates to help with some kind of job?

5. Much of the criminal work we see committed across this trailer has something of a military feel to it. We later see Jason on a helicopter, dressed in a bulletproof vest and demonstrating a very professional demeanor. He’s joined by a dog, potentially pointing to not just Jason having a pet, but also being able to use them as some kind of working dog. Later shots also show Jason confidently disembarking a chopper and checking the chambered round in his rifle – all small details, but ones that help paint the picture of a deeply competent professional.

6. Lucia may not have Jason’s highly trained background, but it looks like she’ll eventually adopt at least some of his tactics. A minute into the trailer, we can see her dressed in special forced black and equipped with a Shrewsbury rotary grenade launcher, popping explosives into pursuing police vehicles.

7. She’s demolishing those cars from on high, hanging from the side of some kind of cargo net. A few seconds later, we see a helicopter carrying a giant load in a very similar cargo net – it seems likely that these shots are taken from the same mission, and that Lucia will hang from the net before or after it’s been dragged through the side of a skyscraper.

8. The damage caused by the crash is more detailed than anything we’ve seen in prior GTA games, with hundreds of shards of glass erupting from the side of the building. While this shot alone is far from confirmation that the game will feature Battlefield-like destruction tech, it is a flashy insight into just how detailed Rockstar is able to make environmental demolition.

9. That kind of collateral damage is to be expected from crime on the scale that GTA typically depicts, and it seems like this game has no intention of being smaller than GTA 5’s biggest moments. We can see Lucia leaping off a car onto a commercial liner, suggesting something on the same scale as some of Trevor’s airborne antics. This shot is likely the precursor to the scene in the second trailer that shows Lucia fighting in a plane’s hold as its landing gear deploys.

10. The aforementioned chopper mission is probably a heist, but what’s definitely a heist is the bank job we see. This is actually the vault we previously saw in a screenshot we exclusively debuted back in August , complete with the burning bank notes and Lucia with her hair in a ponytail.

11. For that shot, Lucia is joined not by Jason but by another anonymous character. We can’t see their face, but whoever they are, it looks like we won’t be alone when conducting heists. In a later shot we see Lucia accompanied by gunmen disguised as construction workers, suggesting we’ll often be joined by crews of criminals. But will these be supporting characters introduced as part of the story, or NPCs hired to help, akin to how heist crews worked in GTA 5?

12. While stealing physical money is a tried and tested form of securing dosh, there’s a chance that GTA 6 will toy with a more decentralised approach, too. We see a bi-plane flying over Vice City’s beach, its side emblazoned with the logo for “DacityCoin”. That’s presumably some kind of Bitcoin parody, but why is it so prominent in the trailer? Why is there a guy hanging onto the plane’s wing and deploying a bright pink smoke flare? Our theory is that Jason and Lucia will take part in some kind of scam, and this is a stunt to advertise a bogus cryptocurrency.

13. Planes aren’t the only high-speed thrills on show. A little later we see street racing, a side activity we first saw in August’s extended look.

14. Of course, most of GTA’s high-speed driving tends to be a race against the cops. A short car chase sequence sees one of our protagonists behind the wheel of a lime green supercar, fleeing police that arrive from all angles. It seems like every new trailer shows off new cars, and we get a very quick peek at the new Invetero Coquette, which can be glimpsed for a split second – look out for its turquoise-and-pink synthwave paint job.

15. For those who prefer waves to asphalt, you might find more joy in the Shasa, which appears to be a new model of boat for GTA 6. We can see Jason and his buddy Cal working on one, buffing out the paintwork. This seems to be Jason’s reality at the start of the story – with his army days behind him, he’s working as a laborer at Brian’s Marina.

16. Brian’s business looks pretty busy – the rental racks are full of boats and jet skis – but the state of Leonida is home to much bigger companies than local traders. In the background of an early shot we can see a Globe Oil truck. We’ve seen Globe Oil in a couple of other games – you may recognise them from GTA 4, or even Chinatown Wars, in which we used the company’s oil to make fiery molotov cocktails.

17. Talking of fiery, there’s definitely a flame burning between Lucia and Jason, who can be seen on an apartment balcony with a beach view. This is a different safehouse compared to the more humble home we saw in the extended look, suggesting that we’ll be moving up in the world as well as around it.

18. “Are we gonna be okay?” asks Lucia. “We stuck together through everything. We just gotta get through it,” Jason replies, emphasising the on-the-run nature of the couple’s story. They won’t be alone, though, with plenty of other characters here to help them.

19. Hopefully Cal won’t be the sharpest mind on their side. Whenever we’ve seen him in the trailers so far, he’s always presented as a bit of a fool. We get to see him play with a pet snake, offering its forked tongue a peck on the lips.

20. Speaking of reptiles, an iguana can be spotted crossing the road, further reinforcing the variety in wildlife across the state of Leonida. GTA 6 will have an animal spotting system, allowing us to find and catalogue them all.

21. We get another quick look at the rap duo, Real Dimez, made up of Roxy and Bae-Luxe. We don’t yet know too much about them. Could they be friends or foes? We know they are signed to Only Raw Records, club mogul Boobie Ike’s company, but he remains much of a mystery to us, too.

22. Someone we know we won’t want to get on the wrong side of is Mendez, a Vice City Police Department officer, who can be briefly glimpsed in a single shot. He certainly feels like he’ll be one of GTA 6’s major antagonists, cutting a figure similar to Samuel L. Jackson’s Officer Tenpenny in San Andreas.

23. We can see more police as multiple cop cars take the off-road approach to chase their suspect. These belong to Mariana County, a part of the map where the Leonida Keys are found.

24. When not hunting Jason and Lucia, it looks like the police still have plenty on their hands across the state. We get a close-up of what look like heavily tattooed gang members riding in a green car. One of them is sporting ink that reads “EW”; could it be a clue to what this gang is called? Take your guesses now.

25. And are the people sporting balaclavas and dancing around a stockpile of golden AKs part of some odd gang? They’ve either watched Harmony Korine’s Spring Breakers too many times or are just modelling the guns. The camera is peering at them through a digital lens, so maybe this could be a photoshoot or music video for one of Only Raw’s artists?

26. Back on the protagonist’s side, we get to see expert bank robber and a seeming accomplice of Jason and Lucia, Raul Bautista, threatening a man at a construction site. This area looks like it belongs to Schlott Construction, if this sign in the background is anything to go by. That company has appeared on vehicle liveries in GTA Online as part of the Import/Export update, but it looks like it will have more of a physical presence in the world of Leonida.

27. Raul appears to be enjoying his bullying, chomping on some chicken as he stomps on a man. Could this be a bucket from Cluckin’ Bell? If so, they’ve changed the design of their packaging considerably since the GTA San Andreas days, with a look borrowed from their real-life counterpart, KFC, seen here. I’m not sure about the quality of that chicken, though. There doesn’t look like there’s much meat on that drumstick.

28. Jason is clearly more of a thigh man. He can be seen with his love, Lucia, as they help each other get clean in the shower. Nothing else to see here but two people who really care about each other’s hygiene. Such is his commitment to cleanliness that he even wipes the shower down with his hand as Lucia gives him a thank you kiss for helping out. Once more, a little later in the trailer, we get a look at them looking after each other. Lucia is on her tiptoes, presumably so she can reach high enough to wash Jason’s hair for him. Incredibly helpful. I hope her ankle tag is waterproof, otherwise this could all end in disaster.

29. Showering seems like a great idea, because GTA 6 looks like it will be a particularly sweaty game. We’ve heard about Rockstar’s absurdly detailed sweat tech , and now we get to see it in action thanks to a man flexing for us at the gym. I hope we don’t have to fight him.

30. If we do, though, then bringing along some knuckle dusters might be a smart move. We can see Jason popping some on. This melee weapon has appeared in numerous GTAs, but was known as Brass Knuckles back in Vice City when we visited in the 1980s.

31. To take down enemies more than a few feet away, Jason will need different weaponry. We see him holding a sniper rifle, and in the scope’s reflection we can spot a helicopter, ready to be taken down. In an earlier shot in the trailer, we could be witnessing the aftermath of Jason pulling the trigger, as he walks away with a helicopter crashing into a ball of flames behind him. As we know, cool guys don’t look at explosions. We can also spot an earpiece in - you’ll never guess it - his ear. Who’s speaking to him? Presumably not the pilot. Not anymore, at least.

32. While we’re trying to piece bits of story together, the gold dress that Lucia is wearing at the end of this trailer is the same one prominently shown in Trailer 2. It looks like this could all be part of one big mission that starts on a yacht, heads to the Nine1Nine club, where at some point Jason and Lucia have to jump from the roof into its pool. Why do they need to escape? We’ll all get to find out very soon on November 19.

33. Soundtracking the whole trailer is a new single recorded just for the game from French electronic duo Justice, who are also composing the game’s original score. “Flower in a Hurricane” also features the Australian psychedelic touch of Tame Impala, fellow Aussie rock band King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, and American singer-songwriter SZA. We’re yet to see an actual hurricane in all of our looks at GTA 6 so far, but we do know that extreme weather will play a part in the game.

So, that’s what we found. Spot anything we may have missed? Let us know in the comments below. If you’ve missed any of our other trailer breakdowns or deep dives into the world of GTA 6, you can check them out here. Not long to go now. We’re almost there.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: New Marvel's Wolverine Funko Pops Drop Next April – Here’s Where You Can Preorder Them
articles.summary: Three new Wolverine Funko Pops, based on Insomniac's latest game, are up for preorder with a release date of April 18 next year. Here's where you can preorder them.
articles.body:
Marvel's Wolverine is officially joining the Funko Pop lineup next year. Three new figures are now available to preorder - a mini model of Wolverine , one of Logan , and another of Omega Red - for $14.99 a piece. However, you'll have to wait a little while before you can add them to your collectible shelf, as they're slated to be released next year on April 18.

While that release date is still many months away from now, it's worth it to preorder your preferred model ahead of time, just in case they sell out. They certainly look like fun figures to have around if you're a fan of the game, too, and measure just under four inches tall so they won't take up much space.

For fans of Insomniac's latest looking for even more Wolverine goodies to buy, there's also an original soundtrack vinyl available to preorder right now, and the wait for that one isn't quite as long as the Funkos. This bright translucent yellow vinyl is set to drop in a couple months time on December 11, which is perfect timing if you're hoping to grab it as a gift for a Wolverine fan for the holidays, too.

And if you're on the hunt for even more Funko figures to add to your collectibles, there's plenty to look forward to that are set to release this year. Sticking within the realm of Marvel, new Avengers: Doomsday figures were recently announced which are set to drop sometime in November ahead of the film's release, so it's worth keeping an eye out for those.

Of course, there's also Black Friday right around the corner , which is a great opportunity to find figures at a discount. These sales kick off around the middle of November, so it won't be long before you can see what collectible discounts pop up.

Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.
